# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
round of questions the check produces. Without a subagent tool, read the
document as that builder yourself.

<HARD-GATE>
Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the full
description: in chat for a small change, the document for a project.
Building includes writing product code, scaffolding, installing
dependencies, creating projects, and invoking an implementation skill.
Reading and exploring are fine.

Two exceptions. If they opted out of the questions, the skill is done
and the gate goes with it. A spike they said yes to may be built; it
stays labeled throwaway, and keeping what it produced is a new request
that comes back through this gate.

After a project's document is approved, the next step is the plan. For
software, invoke superpowers:writing-plans and no other skill.
</HARD-GATE>

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "I'll offer options to save them effort" | Options steer. Ask them to describe it first. |
| "I'll fill in sensible defaults" | Good. Say them out loud. A default they never heard is one they couldn't reject. |
| "I should explain the process first" | Ask your question. The process shows itself. |
| "They said 'sounds good' to the idea" | Approval covers what you showed them. A description you haven't written isn't approved. |
| "The spike works, I'll keep building on it" | Keeping it is a new request. Back through the gate. |

## Visual Companion

A browser tab for showing mockups, diagrams, and prototypes. It's a
tool, not a mode: accepting it doesn't send every question to the
browser.

**Offer it just-in-time.** Offer it the first time one of the moments
above comes up, never upfront. The offer is its own message with nothing
else in it:

> "This might be easier if I show you. Want me to open a browser tab with some mockups?"

If they decline, stay in text and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per question, ask: would they understand this better by seeing it?**
Mockups, layouts, diagrams, and side-by-side designs go in the browser.
Requirements, scope, tradeoffs, and conceptual choices stay in text. A
question about a UI topic isn't automatically a visual question.

If they accept, read `visual-companion.md` in this directory before
starting the server.

### 1b. CRITICAL FINDING — a second, *undefined* token namespace

A parallel namespace of `--studio-*` tokens is **referenced ~120 times** but is **never declared anywhere in the repository**:

```
--studio-amber   --studio-border  --studio-green   --studio-indigo
--studio-indigo-strong  --studio-muted  --studio-radius  --studio-red
--studio-surface  --studio-text
```

Verified: `git grep -nE '\-\-studio-[a-z-]+\s*:' origin/main --` returns **zero** matches. These are dead tokens — every `var(--studio-indigo)` resolves to nothing. **For your marketing site, this is a gift:** the `--studio-*` family is an *unwritten* design-token spec that the codebase already assumes. I have inferred its intended values from the surrounding CSS (§8) and recommend the marketing site **define them explicitly** using my proposed values.

The most likely intended mapping, derived from adjacent literal values:

| Undefined token | Intended value (inferred) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `--studio-indigo` | `#818cf8` | The literal `#818cf8` is used for exactly this role (`.ui-card__id`, `.changelog-modal__badge`, `.changelog-release__version`) |
| `--studio-indigo-strong` | `#7c7ff5` | `.ui-action--primary:hover { background: #7c7ff5; }` — the hover state of the token-based primary |
| `--studio-text` | `#e2e8f0` | The literal `#e2e8f0` is used for `.ui-bet__value`, `.ui-field dd`, `.ui-quote` — the "body text on dark" role |
| `--studio-muted` | `#94a3b8` | `.ui-tone-bg--neutral { background: #94a3b8; }` — the slate-500 of the Tailwind sub-palette |
| `--studio-border` | `rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.14)` | The `.ui-meter__track` background and `.ui-pill--neutral` family use `rgba(148,163,184,…)` |
| `--studio-surface` | `rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5)` | `.ui-stat { background: rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.5); }` |
| `--studio-radius` | `14px` | `.ui-card { border-radius: 14px; }` |
| `--studio-green` | `#34d399` | The `.ui-pill--positive` family uses `rgba(52, 211, 153, …)` = `#34d399` |
| `--studio-amber` | `#fbbf24` | The `.ui-pill--warning` family uses `rgba(251, 191, 36, …)` = `#fbbf24` |
| `--studio-red` | `#f87171` | The `.ui-pill--critical` family uses `rgba(248, 113, 113, …)` = `#f87171` |

Note the `--studio-*` family is **Tailwind-slate-500/400/900** flavoured, while the canonical `--accent/--muted/--faint` family is **custom-grey** flavoured. The file contains two generations of the design language layered on top of each other (§1e).

### 1e. The file's layered history (important for the marketing site)

`theme.css` is a palimpsest of four generations appended chronologically:

1. **Lines 1–1440** — the original hand-crafted system (`--bg`, `--accent`, `--faint`, `.chat`, `.composer`, `.card`, `.badge`, `.metric`).
2. **Lines 1442–1613** — "Manual data controls" + bell/catch-up.
3. **Lines 1614–2407** — the "Generated surfaces" block (`.ui-*`), which is the **Tailwind-slate-flavoured** generation.
4. **Lines 2409–2608** — Changelog modal ("Steve Jobs Quality").
5. **Lines 2610–2809** — "PR #61 micro-interactions" — the Apple-glass generation, adding the `--ease-*` tokens.
6. **Lines 2810–3094** — "One room: the conversation never leaves the stage" — the **Rail + Lens** generation.

  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.775rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.15s ease, color 0.15s ease, transform 0.15s ease,
    border-color 0.15s ease;
}

.suggestion:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--surface-hover);
  border-color: var(--line-strong);
  color: var(--text);
  transform: translateY(-1px);
}

.suggestion:disabled {
  opacity: 0.5;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

/* Composer */
.composer {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 8px;
  width: 100%;
}

/* Slash-command palette */
.palette {
  position: absolute;
  bottom: calc(100% + 10px);
  left: 0;
  right: 0;
  z-index: 20;
  max-height: min(320px, 46vh);
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 6px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
  border-radius: 14px;
  background: var(--bg-raised);
  box-shadow: 0 24px 50px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.42);
  animation: fade-in 0.12s ease;
}

.palette__item {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  gap: 12px;
  width: 100%;
  padding: 8px 10px;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 9px;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--text);
  text-align: left;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.palette__item.is-active {
  background: var(--surface-hover);
}

.palette__name {
  flex: none;
  width: 84px;
  padding-top: 1px;
  color: #c7c8ff;
  font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace);
  font-size: 0.76rem;
}

.palette__text {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 1px;
  min-width: 0;
}

.palette__label {
  font-size: 0.8rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

.palette__description {
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  line-height: 1.4;
}

.palette__empty {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
}

.composer__shell {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-end;
  gap: 10px;
  padding: 8px 9px 8px 16px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 22px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.035);
  box-shadow: 0 14px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.28);
  transition: border-color 0.16s ease, box-shadow 0.16s ease;
}

.composer__shell:focus-within {
  border-color: rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.42);
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.09), 0 14px 34px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3);
}

.composer__input {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
  max-height: 220px;
  padding: 8px 0;
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
  resize: none;
  outline: none;
}

.composer__input::placeholder {
  color: #6f7480;
}

.composer__actions {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
}

.composer__send {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: 34px;
  height: 34px;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--text);
  color: #0b0c10;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: opacity 0.15s ease, transform 0.15s ease;
}

.composer__send:hover:not(:disabled) {
  transform: translateY(-1px);
}

.composer__send:disabled {
  opacity: 0.3;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

.composer__send--stop {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
  color: var(--text);
}

.composer__hint {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 12px;
  margin: 0 8px;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
}

.composer__hint kbd {
  padding: 1px 4px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 4px;
  font-family: inherit;
  font-size: 0.66rem;
}

.composer__status {
  max-width: 45%;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.composer__status.is-offline {
  color: var(--amber);
}

/* Transcript */
.conversation {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 24px;
  padding: 12px 0 8px;
}

.message {
  display: flex;
  gap: 12px;
  animation: fade-in 0.25s ease;
}

.message--user {
  justify-content: flex-end;
}

.message__bubble {
  max-width: 82%;
  padding: 10px 14px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 18px 18px 6px 18px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.065);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  word-break: break-word;
}

.message--assistant {
  align-items: flex-start;
}

.message__avatar {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  width: 26px;
  height: 26px;
  flex: none;
  margin-top: 3px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: linear-gradient(140deg, #6366f1, #8b5cf6);
  color: #f8f8ff;
}

.message__body {
  flex: 1;
  min-width: 0;
  font-size: 0.92rem;
  line-height: 1.62;
  color: #e8e9ed;
}

.message__actions {
  display: flex;
  gap: 4px;
  margin-top: 6px;
  opacity: 0;
  transition: opacity 0.15s ease;
}

.message:hover .message__actions,
.message:focus-within .message__actions {
  opacity: 1;
}

.quiet-action {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 5px;
  padding: 4px 7px;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 6px;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.quiet-action:hover {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.055);
  color: var(--text);
}

.traces {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 6px;
  margin: 12px 0 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

.trace {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 6px;
  max-width: 100%;
  padding: 3px 9px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.02);
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.71rem;
}

.trace__dot {
  width: 5px;
  height: 5px;
  flex: none;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: var(--accent);
}

.trace__preview {
  max-width: 30ch;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  white-space: nowrap;
  color: var(--muted);
}

.typing {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 9px;
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.87rem;
}

.typing__dots {
  display: inline-flex;
  gap: 3px;
}

.typing__dots i {
  width: 5px;
  height: 5px;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: currentColor;
  animation: dot-pulse 1.2s infinite ease-in-out;
}

.typing__dots i:nth-child(2) {
  animation-delay: 0.15s;
}

.typing__dots i:nth-child(3) {
  animation-delay: 0.3s;
}

.caret {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 7px;
  height: 1em;
  margin-left: 2px;
  border-radius: 1px;
  background: var(--accent);
  vertical-align: text-bottom;
  animation: caret-blink 1s steps(1) infinite;
}

/* Markdown */
.md > *:first-child {
  margin-top: 0;
}

.md > *:last-child {
  margin-bottom: 0;
}

.md-paragraph {
  margin: 0 0 10px;
}

.md-heading {
  margin: 16px 0 8px;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: -0.01em;
}

.md-list {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 4px;
  margin: 0 0 10px;
  padding-left: 20px;
}

.md-code {
  padding: 1px 5px;
  border-radius: 5px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.085);
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.85em;
}

.md-pre {
  margin: 0 0 10px;
  padding: 12px 14px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.35);
  overflow-x: auto;
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.md-pre code {
  font-family: var(--mono);
}

.md-quote {
  margin: 0 0 10px;
  padding-left: 12px;
  border-left: 2px solid var(--line-strong);
  color: var(--muted);
}

.md-rule {
  margin: 14px 0;
  border: 0;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
}

/* Panel content primitives */
.stack {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 14px;
}

.metrics {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  gap: 8px;
}

.metric {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 2px;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: var(--surface);
}

.metric__label {
  font-size: 0.64rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint);
}

.metric__value {
  font-size: 1.25rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em;
}

.chips {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 6px;
}

.chip {
  padding: 4px 10px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.73rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}

.chip:hover {
  color: var(--text);
  border-color: var(--line-strong);
}

.chip.is-on {
  background: var(--surface-hover);
  border-color: var(--line-strong);
  color: var(--text);
}

.cards {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 9px;
}

.card {
  padding: 12px 14px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 14px;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.022);
  transition: border-color 0.15s ease, background 0.15s ease;
}

.card:hover {
  border-color: var(--line-strong);
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.035);
}

.card--hot {
  border-color: rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.28);
  background: rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.045);
}

.card__head {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 8px;
}

.card__id {
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  color: var(--accent);
}

.card__statement {
  margin: 8px 0;
  font-size: 0.885rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.card__meta {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 4px;
  margin: 0 0 8px;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.71rem;
}

.card__meta b {
  color: var(--muted);
  font-weight: 600;
}

.card__evidence {
  margin: 0 0 8px;
  padding-left: 10px;
  border-left: 2px solid var(--line-strong);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.card__actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 4px;
}

.badge {
  padding: 2px 8px;
  border: 1px solid transparent;
  border-radius: 999px;
  font-size: 0.65rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  white-space: nowrap;
}

.badge--amber {
  border-color: rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.3);
  background: rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.12);
  color: var(--amber);
}

.badge--green {
  border-color: rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.25);
  background: rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.1);
  color: var(--green);
}

.badge--blue {
  border-color: rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.3);
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.12);
  color: var(--accent);
}

/* Job map */
.phases {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 5px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

.phase {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 5px;
  padding: 4px 9px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 999px;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
}

.phase__index {
  color: var(--muted);
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.65rem;
}

.steps {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 6px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

.step {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 10px;
  padding: 9px 12px;
  border-left: 2px solid rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.5);
  border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0;
  background: var(--surface);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
}

.step__order {
  flex: none;
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  color: var(--accent);
}

.empty-note {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
}

/* Forms */
.form {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
}

.field {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 5px;
  margin-bottom: 2px;
}

.field label {
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  color: var(--muted);
}

.field__hint {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
  line-height: 1.45;
}

.input,
.select {
  width: 100%;
  padding: 8px 10px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 999px;
  background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25);
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 0.84rem;
}

.input:hover,
.select:hover {
  border-color: var(--line-strong);
}

input[type="range"] {
  width: 100%;
  accent-color: var(--accent);
}

.button {
  padding: 8px 12px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.4);
  border-radius: 9px;
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.16);
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 0.82rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background 0.14s ease;
}

.button:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.26);
}

.button:disabled {
  opacity: 0.45;
  cursor: not-allowed;
}

.button--ghost {
  border-color: var(--line);
  background: transparent;
}

.button--ghost:hover:not(:disabled) {
  background: var(--surface-hover);
}

.button--block {
  width: 100%;
}

.disclosure {
  padding-top: 6px;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--line);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.disclosure summary {
  cursor: pointer;
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  list-style: none;
}

.disclosure summary::-webkit-details-marker {
  display: none;
}

.disclosure summary::before {
  content: "+ ";
  color: var(--faint);
}

.disclosure[open] summary::before {
  content: "− ";
}

.disclosure > * + * {
  margin-top: 10px;
}

.disclosure p {
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.76rem;
  line-height: 1.55;
}

/* Impact */
.before-after {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
  gap: 8px;
}

.compare {
  padding: 11px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 12px;
  font-size: 0.76rem;
}

.compare--before {
  border-color: rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.2);
  background: rgba(239, 68, 68, 0.06);
}

.compare--after {
  border-color: rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.2);
  background: rgba(16, 185, 129, 0.06);
}

.compare__label {
  display: block;
  margin-bottom: 6px;
  font-size: 0.63rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.1em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
  color: var(--faint);
}

.compare ul {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 5px;
  margin: 0;
  padding-left: 15px;
  color: var(--muted);
  line-height: 1.45;
}

.compare b {
  color: var(--text);
  font-weight: 600;
}

.score-preview {
  display: flex;
  align-items: baseline;
  gap: 8px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line);
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: var(--surface);
  font-size: 0.78rem;
  color: var(--faint);
}

.score-preview b {
  color: var(--text);
  font-family: var(--mono);
  font-size: 0.95rem;
}

/* Evidence */
.notice {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 9px 11px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.2);
  border-radius: 10px;
  background: rgba(240, 179, 74, 0.06);
  color: #d6c19b;
  font-size: 0.74rem;
  line-height: 1.5;
}

.evidence {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 11px 13px;
  border-left: 2px solid rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.5);
  border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0;
  background: var(--surface);
}

.evidence figcaption {
  margin-bottom: 5px;
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.72rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

.evidence blockquote {
  margin: 0;
  color: #dfe1e7;
  font-size: 0.83rem;
  font-style: italic;
  line-height: 1.55;
}

.evidence__meta {
  display: block;
  margin-top: 7px;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.68rem;
}

/* Settings */
.settings {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 12px;
}

.settings__title {
  margin: 8px 0 0;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.66rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.1em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}

.connection-list {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 2px;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

.connection-list li {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 8px;
  padding: 6px 8px;
  border-radius: 8px;
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.76rem;
}

.connection-list li:hover {
  background: var(--surface);
}

.connection-list__value {
  margin-left: auto;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.7rem;
}

.settings__actions {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 7px;
}

.muted {
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.72rem;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Toasts                                                             */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.toast-stack {
  position: fixed;
  right: 18px;
  bottom: 18px;
  z-index: 1000;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 8px;
  max-width: 360px;
}

.toast {
  display: flex;
  align-items: flex-start;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 10px;
  padding: 10px 12px;
  border: 1px solid var(--line-strong);
  border-radius: 11px;
  background: rgba(16, 18, 23, 0.96);
  box-shadow: 0 12px 30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45);
  color: var(--text);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.toast--success {
  border-color: rgba(74, 222, 128, 0.4);
}

.toast--error {
  border-color: rgba(248, 113, 113, 0.4);
}

.toast--info {
  border-color: rgba(139, 140, 248, 0.4);
}

.toast button {
  border: 0;
  background: transparent;
  color: var(--faint);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  cursor: pointer;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Error fallback                                                     */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.error-page {
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  min-height: 100dvh;
  padding: 24px;
  background: var(--bg);
}

.error-page__card {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 12px;
  max-width: 440px;
  text-align: center;
}

.error-page__title {
  margin: 0;
  font-size: clamp(1.3rem, 3vw, 1.7rem);
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: -0.02em;
  line-height: 1.25;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Loading + motion                                                   */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.skeleton {
  border-radius: 8px;
  background: linear-gradient(
    90deg,
    rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03) 25%,
    rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08) 50%,
    rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03) 75%
  );
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  animation: shimmer 1.6s infinite ease-in-out;
}

.skeleton--tile {
  height: 58px;
}

.skeleton--line {
  height: 12px;
  margin-bottom: 8px;
}

@keyframes shimmer {
  0% {
    background-position: -200% 0;
  }
  100% {
    background-position: 200% 0;
  }
}

@keyframes hero-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
    transform: translateY(6px);
    filter: blur(2px);
  }
  to {
    opacity: 1;
    transform: translateY(0);
    filter: blur(0);
  }
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Offline                                                            */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
.offline {
  display: flex;
  flex: none;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: space-between;
  gap: 10px 16px;
  margin: 6px 22px 0;
  padding: 10px 14px;
  border: 1px solid rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.24);
  border-radius: 12px;
  background: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.06);
  color: var(--muted);
  font-size: 0.78rem;

# GitHub Pages Marketing Site Design

**Date:** 2026-10-18
**Status:** Approved (design authority delegated to the session designer; all builder-check questions answered)
**Scope:** Single-page customer-facing site in `website/` + GitHub Actions deploy to GitHub Pages

## Intent & Why

`README.md` is the project's front door, and it reads like an engineering changelog — right for
contributors, wrong for the PM or eng lead who clicked a shared link asking "is this real, and is it
worth five minutes?" The site answers why/what/how/when in one scroll, with a Jobsian bar:
ruthless focus, one narrative, one obvious action, craft in type and motion, and honesty as the
brand — the project is an experimental testbed, and the page says so out loud.

The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything: **over-promising on an experimental product is the
one thing Jobs never did — the honest answer is the Jobsian answer.** No dates, no maturity theater,
no CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no screenshots of vaporware.

Definition of done for the build (see plan): PR pushed with all GitHub Actions checks green —
lint (ruff), typecheck (mypy), security (bandit), tests (pytest ×6 packages + `website`), smoke,
and the "CI green" aggregate.

## Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done

**Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a shared link, a search, or a
referral. Skeptical of AI-tool marketing.
> When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to know within one screen whether this is a
> real, runnable thing grounded in a method I respect, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it
> or leave without guilt.

**Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating whether to wire agents to an ODI data source.
> When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint and a copy-paste
> quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without talking to anyone.

**Tertiary — the sharing PM (internal champion).** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
> When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion — credibly and
> soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea instead of from my credibility.

## Messaging Hierarchy

Binding copy contract (tests enforce the marked strings; micro-polish — punctuation-level tweaks —
is builder latitude).

| Level | Copy |
|---|---|
| Eyebrow pill | `Experimental` |
| H1 (hero) | **Your roadmap is a guess.** |
| Hero sub | An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them. |
| Primary CTA | **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run` (local quickstart) |
| Secondary CTA | View on GitHub → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi` |
| Tertiary link | Hosted demo — requires a free Prefect account → Horizon chat URL |
| Footer tagline | Built with outcomes, not guesses. |

**Section 2 — `#problem`, "Opinion is expensive."** Three parallel beats, one line each, each with
a short support line:

1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.

Section closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."

**Section 3 — `#insight`, "Ask for outcomes, not opinions."** Three plain sentences:
1. Outcome-Driven Innovation asks customers how much each desired outcome matters and how satisfied
   they are with it today.
2. The gap between importance and satisfaction is where products win or die.
3. Agentic ODI stores those outcomes, scores them, and serves them to any agent over MCP.

Then: a small CSS/inline-SVG bar visual (Importance vs Satisfaction, gap highlighted, labeled
"Illustrative outcome data"), the formula rendered exactly as the code computes it —
`Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)` (source of truth:
`core/src/core/models.py:27`), and the stat callout: **86%** innovation success rate — *as reported
in ODI literature (Strategyn)*. Plain-text attribution only; no link to the in-repo PDF.

**Section 4 — `#how`, "How it works."** Three steps:
1. **Capture** — jobs, steps, and desired outcomes with importance/satisfaction scores, via CLI,
   connectors, or The Living Studio.
2. **Query** — agents call MCP tools for job maps and opportunity scores at decision time, local or
   hosted.
3. **Steer** — The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact
   Simulation so the team decides from the same picture.

Accompanies: a stylized Studio illustration (real shipped surfaces, marked "Illustrative"), never a
fake screenshot.

**Section 5 — `#run`, "Run it in 60 seconds."** Prerequisites line (Python 3.10+, uv), terminal
block with copy button:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git
cd agentic-odi
uv sync --all-packages
python -m client.run
```

Endpoint chips with copy buttons: MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp` · Studio `http://localhost:8501`.
MCP client config snippet (local only):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" }
  }
}
```

Prose note: hosted credentials come from the maintainers — open an issue. Never invent an auth
scheme we cannot document.

**Section 6 — `#status`, "Honest status."** `Experimental` badge; **What works today** (MCP server
tools for jobs/steps/outcomes/customer outcomes with opportunity scoring; The Living Studio —
Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation, Causal Lineage; CLI `outcomes` +
`connectors`; MCP ingest connector; hosted test endpoints requiring auth) and **What's next**
(curated from the README roadmap at build time: map ingested evidence onto ODI artifacts, more
connector kinds, ODI schema definition, context tooling, persistence layer, agentic integration).
Standing line: "We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does." Closer: "Questions?
Open an issue." → Issues link.

**Footer.** Mark + wordmark, tagline, links (GitHub, Issues, Hosted demo), legal line:
`© 2026 Agentic ODI maintainers · All rights reserved` + one-line experimental reminder.

**Voice rules:** warm, direct, second person; plain language; no jargon dumps; **no emoji anywhere
on the site** (house copy rule from the first-run onboarding spec — README's emoji style stays in
README); no superlatives ("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"); English only.

## Information Architecture / Sitemap

| Route | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | `website/index.html` | The entire site. One scroll, seven sections. |
| `/404.html` | `website/404.html` | On-brand, **self-contained** (inline styles, absolute link home) so it renders at any depth on project Pages. |

- Sticky compact header: mark + wordmark (left), single CTA "Run it in 60 seconds" (right). No nav
  links — one page needs no navigation, but the one obvious action must stay reachable.
- In-page anchors: `#problem`, `#insight`, `#how`, `#run`, `#status`.
- No sitemap.xml, no robots.txt, no blog, no docs pages, no search.

## Visual Direction

**Type.** No webfonts, zero downloads:
- `--font-sans: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`
  (same stack The Living Studio ships, `client/src/client/app.py:36`)
- `--font-mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace`

| Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | `clamp(2.75rem, 6.5vw, 4.75rem)` | 700, `-0.02em`, lh 1.05 |
| H2 | `clamp(1.75rem, 3.2vw, 2.5rem)` | 700, `-0.015em`, lh 1.15 |
| H3 / beats | `1.25rem` | 600, lh 1.3 |
| Body / lead | `1.0625rem` (17px) / `1.1875rem` | 400, lh 1.6 |
| Eyebrow, badges | `0.75rem` | 600, `0.08em`, uppercase |
| Code | `0.9375rem` mono | lh 1.55 |

**Color.** Tokens as CSS custom properties; `:root` = light, `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)`
overrides. Palette echoes the shipped Studio dark-glass theme (`#0B0D13` / `#131722` / `#F1F5F9`
straight from `app.py`). All ratios measured, WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥ 4.5:1):

| Token | Light | Dark | Contrast (light / dark) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | `#ffffff` | `#0b0d13` | — |
| `--surface` | `#f5f5f7` | `#131722` | — |
| `--text` | `#1d1d1f` | `#f1f5f9` | 16.8 on bg / 17.7 on bg |
| `--muted` | `#6e6e73` | `#94a3b8` | 5.07 bg, 4.66 surface / 7.58 bg, 6.98 surface |
| `--accent` (button fill, white label) | `#0071e3` | `#0071e3` | white on it: 4.70 (both) |
| `--accent-text` (link text) | `#0062c4` | `#409cff` | 5.93 bg, 5.44 surface / 6.86 bg, 6.32 surface |
| `--accent-hover` | `#0059b8` | `#0059b8` | white on it: 6.73 |
| `--badge` (fg on bg) | `#475569` on `#e2e8f0` | `#cbd5e1` on `#1e293b` | 6.15 / 9.85 |
| `--border` | `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` | `rgba(148,163,184,.16)` | decorative only |

Code blocks are dark (`#0b0d13`) in both schemes — a terminal is a terminal (17.7:1 either way).
OG card is fixed dark, self-contained.

**Layout & spacing.** Mobile-first; content max-width 1080px, prose max-width 68ch; inline padding
`clamp(20px, 5vw, 40px)`; section padding-block `clamp(72px, 12vw, 140px)`; 8px spacing scale as
custom properties; radius 12px cards / 999px pills (echoing the Studio's own radii); 1px hairline
borders. Beats and steps go two-column at ≥720px.

**Motion.** Restrained, explanatory, never load-bearing:
- Hero stagger on load: eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, 12px fade-up, 60ms stagger, 400ms,
  `cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1)` — pure CSS, no JS.
- Scroll reveal: sections fade-up once when 15% visible (IntersectionObserver). Default state is
  **visible**; JS opts content into the hidden-then-reveal state only after it loads, so no-JS
  readers never see hidden content.
- Buttons: 150ms `background-color`/`transform`, hover `translateY(-1px)`, active `scale(.98)`.
- Copy button swaps its label to "Copied" for 1.5s, announced via an `aria-live="polite"` span.
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: all transforms/stagger removed, reveals off, content
  immediate.

**Imagery & assets (none exist in the repo — all created):**
- **Mark** (`mark.svg`, hand-authored, viewBox `0 0 32 32`): rounded-square canvas with an
  ascending two-step polyline and a filled dot at the apex — the opportunity curve breaking
  upward. Accent stroke `#0071e3`, hairline frame. Works at 16px, single color-safe.
- **Favicon:** `favicon.svg` (same geometry) + `favicon.png` 32×32 (generated, dark tile, for
  browsers that ignore SVG icons).
- **Opportunity visual:** pure CSS/inline SVG bars in `#insight`, `aria`-labeled, marked
  "Illustrative outcome data".
- **Studio illustration:** stylized abstraction of shipped surfaces only (Opportunity Landscape,
  Universal Job Map, Impact Simulation — verified in `client/src/client/app.py:683-838`), marked
  "Illustrative". Depicting vaporware on a page whose thesis is "no guesses" would self-destruct.
- All decorative SVGs `aria-hidden="true"`; no stock photos, no icon fonts, no emoji.

## Content Sources

| Content | Source | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Quickstart commands (`uv sync --all-packages`, `python -m client.run`) | README §Getting Started — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Local endpoints (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`, `http://localhost:8501`) | README One-Command Launch — **verbatim** | `test_readme_sync.py` |
| Hosted chat URL | README §Deployment — **verbatim**; the label "requires a free Prefect account" is fresh | `test_readme_sync.py` + allowlist |
| Experimental framing, maturity claims | README banner — adapted, no new claims | review + honesty tests |
| What works today / What's next | README roadmap checkboxes, curated at build time (re-read README in Task 2 of the plan) | review focus |
| License/legal line | README §License — adapted ("All rights reserved") | honesty test |
| 86% stat + "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)" | Session decision (no link to `knowledge/*.pdf`) | honesty test |
| Opportunity formula | `core/src/core/models.py:27-29` | formula test |
| Headline, subhead, beats, section titles, CTA labels, tagline, OG copy | **Written fresh** — binding in this spec | structural tests |
| Mark, favicon, illustrations, OG art | Created per this spec | asset tests |

Rule: README is the source of truth for every command, URL, and status claim. If the page and
README disagree, the page is wrong.

## Technical Approach

Hand-crafted static HTML + one CSS file + ≤100 lines of vanilla JS. **No framework** (no
Astro/Next/React): one page with no routing, no state, no data, no components shared across
views — a framework buys a toolchain, a lockfile, hydration, and an upgrade treadmill, and charges
rent on every one of them. Consequence of no framework: deploy is "copy files", the review diff is
readable HTML, Lighthouse is high by construction, and there is zero supply chain on the page.

```
website/
  index.html            # the site
  404.html              # self-contained fallback
  assets/
    style.css           # tokens + full design system (no external URLs)
    main.js             # ≤100 lines: reveal + copy buttons, defer, progressive enhancement
    mark.svg  favicon.svg
    og.png    favicon.png   # committed, generated (see OG strategy)
  tools/
    make_og.py          # regenerates og.png + favicon.png (Pillow, pinned)
  tests/
    test_site.py  test_assets.py  test_make_og.py
    test_workflows.py  test_readme_sync.py
```

- **Paths:** every in-page URL is **relative** (`assets/…`, `#anchor`) so the site works under the
  project-Pages base `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future custom domain.
  `og:url` / `og:image` / `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
- Local preview: `python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory website` (preview the 404 by opening
  `/404.html` directly — `http.server` serves its own 404).
- JS is `defer`'d and additive: the page is complete, styled, and readable with JS disabled.
- Python tooling lives only in `tools/` + `tests/`, run from the repo root with the workspace venv.

## OG / Social Strategy

Social previews are the main earned-distribution artifact — one committed raster, no mystery binary.

- `website/assets/og.png`: **1200×630**, fixed dark card — mark + "Agentic ODI" wordmark,
  headline "Your roadmap is a guess.", sub "Verified customer outcomes, jobs, and opportunity
  scores — served over MCP.", bottom row `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi` + Experimental badge.
- `website/tools/make_og.py`: the committed, runnable generator (stdlib argparse + Pillow). Writes
  `og.png` and `favicon.png`; defaults embed the canonical card copy above. Deterministic output —
  fixed palette/positions, no timestamps, `compress_level=9`, font via
  `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` (Pillow's embedded Aileron, SIL OFL — no font file in the repo).
  Run: `uv run python website/tools/make_og.py`.
- **Regenerability is enforced:** `test_make_og.py` renders fresh bytes and asserts they are
  pixel-identical to the committed PNGs. Change the script → the test fails until you regenerate.
  Change the card copy → defaults in the script are the source.
- Meta contract on `index.html`: `og:type=website`, `og:site_name`, `og:title`
  ("Your roadmap is a guess. — Agentic ODI"), `og:description`, `og:url` (canonical Pages URL),
  `og:image` (absolute PNG URL), `twitter:card=summary_large_image` + title/description/image,
  `rel=canonical`, `theme-color` per color scheme, both favicons. Title tag ≤ 60 chars:
  `Agentic ODI — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes`.
- og:image is never loaded by the page itself (page weight unaffected).
- No OpenGraph on SVG: scrapers (X, LinkedIn, Slack, iMessage) need raster — hence exactly one PNG.

## Deploy Pipeline

**`.github/workflows/pages.yml`** (deploy only — its contract is tested in `ci.yml` via
`test_workflows.py`, so PRs validate it without triggering a deploy):

- `on: push branches [main] paths [website/**, .github/workflows/pages.yml]`, plus
  `workflow_dispatch`.
- Workflow permissions: `contents: read`, `pages: write`, `id-token: write`. Concurrency:
  `group: pages`, `cancel-in-progress: false`. Environment: `github-pages` (URL from the
  deployment step).
- Job `deploy`, steps: checkout@v7 → `./.github/actions/setup` → **run
  `uv run pytest website/tests -q` (verify before publish)** → `actions/configure-pages@v6` →
  stage the artifact with
  `mkdir -p _site && rsync -a --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/ website/ _site/` →
  `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v5` (`path: _site`) → `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
  Only the site publishes — tests and generator never do; `_site/` is CI-only and gitignored.
- **Manual gate:** repository Settings → Pages → Source = "GitHub Actions" must be set **before
  this workflow first runs on `main`**, or the deploy job fails. (One-time toggle; flag before
  merge.)

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**: add a `website` job (setup + `uv run pytest website/tests -q`,
timeout 10m) and add `website` to `ci-green`'s `needs`. Root `ruff check .` / `ruff format --check .`
already cover `website/**` once root ruff config exists (below).

## Accessibility & Performance Budget

**Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA):**
- Semantic landmarks (`header`/`main`/`footer`), one `h1`, no skipped heading levels, `lang="en"`.
- Contrast: measured pairs in the color table — every text pair ≥ 4.5:1 in both schemes.
- Full keyboard operability; visible focus ring (≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors); copy controls are
  real `<button>`s with accessible names; `aria-live` for "Copied".
- Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful links (no "click here"); `prefers-reduced-motion`
  respected; viewport meta; tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.

**Performance:**
- Zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, zero analytics, zero cookies — the page talks only to
  its own origin.
- Weights (raw, committed): HTML ≤ 60 KB, CSS ≤ 30 KB, JS ≤ 4 KB (≤ 100 non-blank lines), each SVG
  ≤ 10 KB, `favicon.png` ≤ 5 KB, total transferred ≤ 150 KB; `og.png` ≤ 300 KB (test-enforced;
  expected ~15–40 KB).
- Lighthouse ≥ 95 on Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO (mobile emulation,
  manual run before merge — CI has no browser).

## Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

- **Not a docs site, not a blog.** No MkDocs/Docusaurus, no nav maze, no search, no sitemap.
- **No framework, no build step, no dependencies on the deployed artifact.**
- **No claims the repo can't back:** no dates or milestones; no "open source" or license claim
  (repo is all-rights-reserved); no maturity language beyond the Experimental framing; no invented
  testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmark numbers; no emoji.
- **No dead ends:** no CTAs behind auth (hosted is tertiary, labeled); no personal emails, no
  invented Discord/Slack; access channel = GitHub Issues only.
- **No auth fiction:** local MCP config only; never link the 401 `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app`
  endpoint as something a visitor can try; no invented header/token scheme.
- **No vaporware imagery:** Studio illustration is abstraction-of-shipped-surfaces, labeled
  "Illustrative"; no fake screenshots.
- **No hotlinking `knowledge/Strategyn_*.pdf`** — attribution text only.
- **No analytics/cookies/CDN/fonts/i18n** — scope is English, one page, two schemes.
- **No publishing dev files:** `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.

## Risks & Mitigations

1. **Pages not enabled before first merge** → deploy job red on `main`. Mitigation: manual toggle
   flagged as a pre-merge gate in the plan's final task.
2. **README drift** (commands/URLs change, page rots) → `test_readme_sync.py` fails CI.
3. **Committed PNG drifts from generator** → pixel-identity test fails CI until regeneration.
4. **Scope creep** (nav items, extra pages, webfonts) → anti-goals + structural tests (allowlisted
   links, weight budgets) push back mechanically.
5. **Ruff newly covers `website/**`** → root config added at repo-consistent line length; commit
   steps run root lint/format parity before every commit.

## Resolved Questions (builder-check × session — all settled)

1. **Primary CTA** → local quickstart ("Run it in 60 seconds"). Verified live: Horizon chat 302s
   to `auth.horizon.prefect.io`, hosted MCP returns 401 — a hero CTA that dead-ends anonymous
   visitors in auth is malpractice. Hosted is tertiary, labeled "requires a free Prefect account."
2. **Access channel** → GitHub Issues (footer + status section). No personal email, no invented
   Discord.
3. **MCP snippet** → local config only (`http://localhost:8000/mcp`); hosted credentials are
   requested via issues. Never document an auth scheme we don't have.
4. **OG image** → one committed PNG, regenerated by committed `website/tools/make_og.py`
   (deterministic, tested pixel-identical). SVG-only cards render poorly on X/LinkedIn/iMessage.
5. **"When"** → no dates. "What works today / What's next" under an explicit Experimental badge,
   mirroring the README roadmap.
6. **Living Studio visual** → stylized abstraction grounded in real shipped surfaces, labeled
   "Illustrative" — never a fake screenshot.
7. **86% stat** → plain-text attribution "as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)"; no link to
   the copyrighted in-repo PDF.

## Builder Calls (design authority — beyond the session's settled six)

1. **Formula corrected to repo truth:** the session sketch showed `Opportunity = Importance −
   Satisfaction`; the code computes `importance + max(importance − satisfaction, 0)`
   (`core/src/core/models.py:28`). The page shows the real formula, and a test pins page ↔ code.
2. **OG renderer = Pillow, pinned in root dev deps** (`pillow==12.3.0`, `uv.lock` updated):
   `ImageFont.load_default(size=…)` ships the Aileron font inside Pillow — real typography, no font
   binary, deterministic bytes, zero deploy-time dependency (Pillow never ships to Pages).
   Generator also emits `favicon.png`.
3. **Full color/type/motion system specified with measured contrast ratios** (table above); palette
   lifted from the shipped Studio theme for brand continuity.
4. **Sticky compact header** (wordmark + one CTA), no nav links.
5. **`404.html` included, self-contained** — absolute home link + inline styles, because relative
   assets break when Pages serves 404.html at arbitrary depths under the `/agentic-odi/` base.
6. **Relative assets + absolute canonical/OG URLs** — required by GitHub project-Pages base path.
7. **Test/CI architecture:** `website/tests/` run by a new `website` job in `ci.yml` (added to
   `ci-green` needs) *and* as a verify-before-publish step inside the Pages deploy job; workflow
   YAML itself is contract-tested with PyYAML (`pyyaml==6.0.3` declared in root dev deps).
8. **Artifact staging** via `rsync --exclude tests/ --exclude tools/` → `_site/` (CI-only,
   gitignored): the published site is the site, nothing else.
9. **Root `[tool.ruff]` added** (line-length 100, target py310, select `E4,E7,E9,F,I,UP,B,BLE`,
   mirroring `cli/pyproject.toml`) so `website/**` Python is linted at repo standards — verified
   impact is website-only (no other root-level `.py` files exist).
10. **Hosted link = Horizon chat only**; the `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is never linked
    (401) — it is mentioned only as "credentials via an issue."
11. **Closed external-link allowlist** (repo, Issues, Horizon chat, uv docs, MCP docs, canonical);
    no analytics, no sitemap/robots/JSON-LD — SEO comes from meta + structure alone.
12. **No emoji on the site** (README's emoji vocabulary stays in README).
13. **Pages source toggle is a pre-merge gate**, not a post-merge note — without it `main` goes red.

## What's Left to the Builder

Exact micro-copy polish within the binding strings above; section/illustration composition and grid
details; animation timing fine-tuning within the stated curves; favicon/mark geometry drafting within
the stated concept; breakpoint tuning; workflow YAML details not specified (names, step ordering).

Research complete. Here's what I found:

**The site is 57 commits stale — and factually wrong about the product.**

| Site says | Reality (on `main` today) |
|---|---|
| "Hosted demo" → `horizon.prefect.io` | **Dead.** 307 → WorkOS sign-in wall. The endpoint no longer exists. |
| "requires a free Prefect account" | Wrong. Product moved to **Cloudflare Workers** (live, 200 OK). README mentions Prefect **0 times**. |
| Studio = "Opportunity Landscape, Job Map, Impact Simulation" | Now a **chat-first app**: one room, transcript + composer never leave the screen, agent composes inline surfaces, Rail + Lens, first-run wizard, 17 connector presets, Tauri desktop app, 30 MCP tools. |
| 5 text sections, 64ch column | A dark glassmorphic product (`#0a0b0e`, indigo `#8b8cf8`, Apple easings). The site shares **none** of its DNA. |

Also broken today: copy button is dead (`.copy_btn` vs `.copy-btn`), `.revealed` never defined, dark mode breaks (inline hex), `<title>` is `"Agentic ODI — Agentic ODI"`, meta description truncated mid-sentence, `<h1>` sits above `<header>`, and three conflicting color palettes.

I have everything I need. Here's the plan.

---

# Redesign Plan — Agentic ODI GitHub Pages

## 0. Answering the architecture question directly

**GitHub Pages has no runtime.** The constraint is on the *output* (static files), not the *tooling*. A build step runs in Actions, then uploads the artifact. So all three paths are Pages-legal. The real question is which produces the best result for this repo:

| Path | Output | npm in Pages CI | Anti-drift for MCP tools / CLI / connectors? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hand-written HTML | static | no | ❌ drifts immediately |
| Astro | static | yes | ❌ still needs a Python extraction step → JSON handoff |
| **Python generator → static** | static | **no** | ✅ built in |

**Recommendation: a Python static-site generator, no Node in the Pages path.** The decisive reason: the docs hub's reference content (30 MCP tools, CLI command tree, 17 connectors, ODI schema) lives in **Python source**. Astro/Vite would *still* need a Python script to extract it and then hand JSON to a second toolchain. One language, one lockfile, one CI path.

**The Studio keeps React 19 + Vite + TypeScript, untouched.** Zero required change.

This also mirrors a pattern the repo already proved: `make_og.py` → committed `og.png` → pytest asserts pixel-identity. The same pattern scales to the whole site.

### Concrete reuse (your "bonus" — and it's a big one)

| Site content | Source of truth | Drift possible? |
|---|---|---|
| MCP tool reference (30 tools) | `packages/core/.../contract.py` `TOOL_SPECS` (already contract-tested vs. live FastMCP) | No — generated |
| Connector catalog (17 presets) | `packages/connectors/.../catalog.py` | No |
| ODI entity JSON schema | `packages/core/.../schema.py` | No |
| Opportunity formula | `packages/core/.../models.py` | No (already test-pinned) |
| CLI command tree | `apps/cli/.../cli.py` (Typer registry) | No |
| All guide prose | `docs/*.md` verbatim | No — one source |
| Palette, type, radii, easings | `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` | No — **one-way read, Studio unchanged** |
| Install / quickstart | `README.md` | No |

---

## 1. Design system (the DNA)

Dark-only, matching the shipped Studio so the site and product are visually inseparable.

```css
--bg:#0a0b0e; --bg-raised:#0e1014; --bg-sunken:#060709;
--text:#f1f2f4; --muted:#a2a7b3; --faint:#71767f;
--accent:#8b8cf8; --accent-strong:#6366f1;
--green:#4ade80; --amber:#f0b34a; --red:#f87171;
--line:rgba(255,255,255,.07); --line-strong:rgba(255,255,255,.14);
--surface:rgba(255,255,255,.03); --surface-hover:rgba(255,255,255,.06);
--glass:rgba(255,255,255,.045);
--ease-out:cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1);
--ease-spring:cubic-bezier(.175,.885,.32,1.22);
--ease-tactile:cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1);
```

**Type** — display `clamp(2.75rem,7.5vw,6rem)` / 600 / `-0.04em` / lh .98 · H2 `clamp(1.875rem,4vw,3.25rem)` / 600 / `-0.03em` · H3 `clamp(1.25rem,2vw,1.75rem)` / 600 · lead `clamp(1.0625rem,1.5vw,1.375rem)` / muted · body `1.0625rem`/1.65 · eyebrow `0.6875rem`/600/`0.18em`/uppercase. Zero webfonts.

**Signature moves** (Apple-grade, not gimmicks):
1. The Studio's own two radial indigo gradients on the canvas — depth with zero imagery
2. Glass panels: `blur(20px) saturate(180%)` + `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.06)` top highlight
3. Scroll-linked "lens" reveals — surfaces dock beside the narrative (the Studio's own Rail+Lens metaphor, applied to the page)
4. The ODI formula as a real typographic equation with the gap term in accent, gap bar animating on scroll
5. **Pixel-faithful renders of the six shipped ODI cards** (outcome-card, opportunity-board, impact-simulation, evidence-quote, job-map, decision-record) — this replaces "no screenshots exist" with a real product gallery
6. Terminal-dark code panels with working copy buttons

---

## 2. Information architecture

```
/                      landing
/docs/                 hub index
/docs/cli/             ← docs/cli.md
/docs/mcp/             ← GENERATED from contract.py + live registry
/docs/connectors/      ← docs/connectors.md + generated preset table
/docs/studio/          ← docs/living-studio.md
/docs/architecture/    ← docs/architecture/README.md + data-flow.md
/docs/deployment/      ← docs/deployment.md
/docs/installation/    ← docs/installation.md
/docs/local-llm/       ← docs/local-llm.md
/docs/development/     ← docs/development.md
/docs/roadmap/         ← docs/roadmap.md
/404.html              self-contained
/sitemap.xml  /robots.txt
```

Each docs page carries a **"Source of truth: `docs/cli.md` — view on GitHub"** link, so the repo stays visibly authoritative.

---

## 3. Landing page narrative (PM first, then dev)

| # | Section | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Hero** | `Experimental` pill · **"Your roadmap is a guess."** · sub · "Run it in 60 seconds" + "Open the Living Studio" |
| 2 | **The Living Studio** | **Interactive scripted demo** in a device frame — the centerpiece |
| 3 | **Opinion is expensive.** | The three existing beats, unchanged |
| 4 | **Ask for outcomes, not opinions.** | The formula + animated importance/satisfaction gap viz + 86% Strategyn attribution |
| 5 | **The surfaces** | The six ODI cards rendered for real |
| 6 | **How it works** | Capture / Query / Steer, rewritten for the chat-first product |
| 7 | **Bring your own tools** | 17 connector presets |
| 8 | **Run it in 60 seconds** | Install tabs (uv / prebuilt binary) + MCP config + endpoint chips |
| 9 | **The MCP surface** | Peek at the 30 tools → link to full reference |
| 10 | **Experimental** | What works today / what's next — *no dates* |
| 11 | **Footer** | Mark, wordmark, tagline, links, legal |

### The demo (section 2)

A pixel-faithful recreation of the Studio's chat surface inside a subtle device frame: the `.bar` with brand + health pill, the transcript, the pill composer. Three scripted exchanges — *capture a complaint → outcome-card*, *"which bet?" → opportunity-board*, *"show me the job" → job-map* — with the agent typing (blinking caret), then the surface materializing on `--ease-spring`. Suggestion chips are real `<button>`s.

**Honesty (non-negotiable):** labelled "Scripted preview — canned responses. The live Studio talks to a real MCP server," with a link to the live hosted Studio. No network calls, no analytics, works offline, and **degrades to a static readable transcript with JS off**.

---

## 4. Repository shape

```
website/
  templates/     base.html  landing.html  doc.html  reference.html
  content/       landing copy (structured)
  assets/        style.css  tokens.css(generated)  main.js  demo.js  mark.svg
  tools/         build_site.py  extract.py  make_og.py
  tests/         test_site.py  test_design_system.py  test_generated.py
                 test_content_sync.py  test_make_og.py  test_pages_deploy.py
  dist/          ← generated output (committed, drift-gated)
```

`build_site.py` renders `dist/` deterministically; CI asserts the committed output matches a fresh build (same pattern as `og.png`). Deps added to root dev group: `jinja2`, `markdown-it-py`, `pygments` — all pure-Python, build-time only, never shipped.

**CI:** `ci.yml` website job gains a drift check; `pages.yml` runs pytest → build → rsync `website/dist/ _site/` → upload → deploy. `sync-readme.py` is retired (replaced by the generator).

---

## 5. Test contract (rewritten)

- `test_site.py` — per-page structure, meta, one `h1`, landmarks, anchors, honesty strings, no dates, no emoji, external-link allowlist
- `test_design_system.py` — tokens, type scale, motion, `focus-visible`, reduced-motion
- `test_generated.py` — build determinism + committed output freshness
- `test_content_sync.py` — **site's tool list ≡ `contract.py`; presets ≡ `catalog.py`; CLI ≡ Typer; formula ≡ `models.py`**
- `test_make_og.py` — kept, repainted to the new palette
- `test_pages_deploy.py` — updated for the build step

**A11y/perf budget:** WCAG 2.1 AA (text ≥4.5:1, UI ≥3:1), skip link, full keyboard operability, reduced-motion honored, zero third-party requests, zero webfonts, ≤200 KB transfer/page, Lighthouse ≥95 all categories.

---

## 6. Phases

1. **Foundation** — tokens, generator skeleton, layout primitives, 404, sitemap/robots
2. **Landing** — hero → insight, with the animated ODI gap
3. **The demo** — Studio frame, scripted surfaces, no-JS fallback
4. **Surfaces gallery** — the six cards, pixel-faithful
5. **Docs hub** — markdown rendering, nav, 10 pages
6. **Generated reference** — MCP tools, connectors, CLI, schema
7. **OG/social + polish** — new card art, favicon, motion pass, a11y pass
8. **CI/deploy** — drift gate, Pages workflow, README sync

**Risks:** the `docs/deployment.md` I read is *itself* stale (still names Horizon Prefect as the MCP host) — the docs hub will surface that; I'd fix the doc in the same pass. Jinja2 is the only new runtime dep. The docs-hub markdown pipeline (tables, fenced code, anchors) is the fiddliest build step.

---

Three decisions left that change the build:

options.description: Keep the H1, the sub, and the three problem beats verbatim (tests + spec pin them). Rewrite only 'How it works' and 'Status', which are now factually stale - the Studio is chat-first with 17 connectors and a desktop app, and the hosted service moved to Cloudflare.
options.label: Keep thesis, refresh stale sections (Recommended)

options.description: Keep everything as-is, including the older framing. The 'How it works' and 'Status' copy stays generic enough not to be wrong, but says less than the product deserves.

options.description: Re-derive the whole narrative around the chat-first Studio - 'One room. Ask it like a colleague.' Risk: loses the strongest line in the project and breaks the pinned honesty contract strings.

# Deployment

## Project Site (GitHub Pages)

The static site in `website/` is published to
**[https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**
by [`.github/workflows/pages.yml`](../.github/workflows/pages.yml).

- A push to `main` runs the website tests, builds `_site` from `website/`, and
  deploys the artifact with `actions/deploy-pages`.
- `workflow_dispatch` republishes the site from the Actions tab without a code
  change.
- Pages is configured with the "GitHub Actions" source, so there is no
  `gh-pages` branch. Removing `pages.yml` stops all publishing and the site
  returns 404.
- The `github-pages` environment only allows deployments from `main`.

## Hosted MCP Server

The server is deployed via **[Horizon Prefect](https://www.prefect.io/horizon)**,
Prefect's managed infrastructure for hosting MCP-compatible agents.

## Test Chat (UI)

Interact with the deployed agent directly in your browser:

> **[https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat](https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat)**

## MCP Server Endpoint

Integrate via the MCP protocol at:

> **[https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp](https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp)**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Authentication is required** to access the MCP server endpoint. Please reach
> out to the maintainers to obtain the necessary credentials before connecting a
> client.

## Hosted Studio

The Living Studio SPA is deployed to Cloudflare Workers:

| Environment | URL |
|---|---|
| Production (`main`) | **[https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)** |
| Pull request preview | Posted automatically by Cloudflare Workers Builds as a PR comment |

Production deploys on every push to `main`. The Worker is `agentic-odi`; keep
`name` in `wrangler.jsonc` aligned with the Worker connected in the dashboard.
Preview builds run for non-production branches and are ephemeral: the Cloudflare
PR comment is the source of truth, so do not copy a preview URL into docs. The
hosted UI loads without a backend; canvas data, chat, and mutations need the
sidecar tunnel described below.

## Living Studio on a Free Cloudflare Worker

Workers Containers — the only way to run the Python sidecar entirely on
Cloudflare — requires the Workers Paid plan. On the free plan, the Worker serves
the built SPA as Workers Static Assets and proxies `/api/*` to the sidecar
through a free, account-less
[Cloudflare Quick Tunnel](https://developers.cloudflare.com/tunnel/get-started/quick-tunnels/).

`wrangler.jsonc` publishes `apps/studio/dist` with SPA fallback and runs the Worker
first for `/api/*`; `infra/cloudflare/worker.ts` forwards those calls to the
`SIDECAR_URL` secret. The browser only talks to the Worker origin, so the
sidecar's CORS list is not involved.

```bash
# 1. Build the SPA that the Worker uploads as static assets
npm --prefix apps/studio ci
npm --prefix apps/studio run build

# 2. Terminal A — MCP server (:8000) + sidecar (:8100)
python scripts/dev.py

# 3. Terminal B — free public URL for the sidecar (no account required)
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8100
# copy the https://<random>.trycloudflare.com URL it prints

# 4. Store the URL on the Worker, then deploy
npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL   # paste the trycloudflare URL
npx wrangler deploy
```

Workers Builds settings (Workers & Pages → your Worker → Settings → Builds):

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Production branch | `main` |
| Root directory | `/` |
| Build command | `npm --prefix apps/studio ci && npm --prefix apps/studio run build` |
| Deploy command | `npx wrangler deploy` |
| Preview command | `npx wrangler preview` |

A Worker has no run command: the Worker script runs on Cloudflare. Set `name` in
`wrangler.jsonc` to the Worker you created before the first deploy.

### Pull request previews

Workers Builds posts the build status and Preview URL to the pull request
automatically. To enable it:

1. Open the Worker → **Settings** → **Build** → **Branch control**.
2. Keep the production branch set to `main` and enable **Preview Builds**.
3. If Cloudflare shows **Set up Worker Previews**, complete the one-time switch.
   This cannot be reversed.
4. Confirm the Preview command is `npx wrangler preview`.

`wrangler.jsonc` must keep a `previews` block, even an empty one: the
`wrangler preview` command fails the build with "Your Wrangler configuration is
missing a `previews` block" without it. Assets and compatibility settings stay
at the top level, so `"previews": {}` is enough while Previews need no extra
settings. If a future Preview needs vars or bindings, add them under `previews`
with Preview-safe values.

Previews do not inherit production settings. The SPA loads from a Preview, but
`/api/*` returns `502 SIDECAR_URL is not configured` until a preview-specific
`SIDECAR_URL` secret is configured:

```bash
npx wrangler preview secret put SIDECAR_URL --name <branch>
```

When `--name` is omitted it defaults to the current git branch. Previews are
ephemeral, and pull requests from forks may not receive one. If Cloudflare does
not comment, paste the URL into the PR's **Deployment** section.

The `cf` CLI can inspect build triggers and recent builds (`cf builds triggers
list`, `cf builds list`) and create a Preview (`cf previews deploy`), but it does
not post GitHub PR comments. The Workers Builds Git integration owns the PR link;
`cf` is only an optional verification tool and requires `cf auth login`.

> [!NOTE]
> The sidecar runs on your machine, so the Worker only works while
> `python scripts/dev.py` and the Quick Tunnel are running. Quick Tunnel URLs
> change on every restart — update the secret with
> `npx wrangler secret put SIDECAR_URL`. Chat also needs a reachable
> OpenAI-compatible endpoint in the Studio's **Settings**; the canvas, job map,
> and impact simulation work without one.

# Intent-First PM Experience Design

**Date:** 2026-10-21
**Status:** Approved for implementation
**Scope:** The Living Studio's first-run flow, conversation, memory, default canvas, and supporting sidecar API.

## Intent & Why

Product managers are judged on the opportunities they choose and the outcomes they deliver. They arrive with an ambition, a mandate, or a vague itch — not with a request for a methodology. The current Studio opens with Outcome-Driven Innovation vocabulary and treats the framework as the destination. That is backwards.

The Studio should be the PM's strategist: it listens for the opportunity they want to chase, translates their intent into rigorous structures underneath, remembers what it learns, and shows its work. ODI remains the engine. It is never the greeting.

**North star:** *Help me choose and win the next opportunity that matters — to my customers, my business, and my career.*

Understanding the business and deciding what to build are stepping stones to that. They are evidence for the opportunity thesis, not the opening question.

## Goals

- Open the first conversation with the PM's ambition, not the framework.
- Make the Opportunity Thesis the central artifact of the product.
- Remember the PM: transcript, durable observations, and the thesis, stored locally.
- Show what the agent learned, as it learns it, with accept/edit/dismiss.
- Remove ODI terminology from default surfaces; keep a deliberate expert view.
- Use warm, direct, encouraging, humble, and thankful copy.
- Isolate demo data so it can never masquerade as the PM's evidence.

## Non-Goals

- Multi-user accounts, cloud sync, or team collaboration.
- A full stakeholder-map or business-case builder in this slice.
- Replacing the MCP domain model or the ODI scoring implementation.
- A complete visual redesign. We reuse the existing design language.
- Automatic LLM extraction independent of the agent's `remember` tool.

## Experience

### First run

One screen, one question:

> **What would make this a year to remember?**
> The opportunity you'd be proud to own. Not a backlog. Not a roadmap.

Four doors:

- I have an opportunity in mind.
- My boss handed me a priority.
- I need to find one.
- Pressure-test an idea.

Connection readiness is a quiet second step: "Let's make sure I can hear you." Technical configuration is collapsed under **Advanced**. The first prompt is written as the PM would speak, not as an ODI request.

### Conversation

The agent asks one question at a time. It starts with the opportunity or the win, then learns about the PM, then the customer, the business, and the people who need to say yes. It reflects back before advising:

> Here's the opportunity I hear… The outcome… The business case… The career case… What I'm still unsure about… Does that sound like your world?

If the PM does not know what to chase, the agent runs a discovery path: what is changing, where the workaround is ugly, what they could uniquely own. It offers three hypotheses, each with why now and why them. Familiar examples and market-gap archetypes are inspiration, never a lecture.

### Canvas

The default view is **Your next move**: the thesis and the opportunities in play. Supporting views:

- **What I've learned** — the memory, editable.
- **The evidence** — customer signals, business data, market context.
- **How the work happens** — the job map, in plain language.
- **What changes if we do this** — the bet simulation.
- **Add what you know** — manual capture, in plain language.
- **Show the ODI view** — the expert layer: outcomes, scores, formula, job stages.
