# GitHub Pages Redesign — The Product Site

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** Approved (session decisions 2026-10-22; all builder questions settled)
**Scope:** `website/` — the public GitHub Pages site for Agentic ODI
**Supersedes:** `2026-10-18-github-pages-design.md` (the single-page era)

---

## Intent & Why

`README.md` is the project's front door for contributors. The Pages site is the front door
for everyone else: a PM who clicked a link, a developer deciding what to wire an agent to,
a skeptic deciding whether this is real.

The 2026-10-18 site answered "is this real?" adequately. It cannot answer "what is this,
what can it do, and how do I use it?" — because the product moved on and the site did not.
The site is now 57 commits behind `main`, and it is **factually wrong in three places**
(section 1). The design goal is no longer "a well-crafted single page"; it is a
**state-of-the-art product site** that carries the full weight of what Agentic ODI now is.

The Jobsian constraint that shapes everything, unchanged: **over-promising on an
experimental product is the one thing Jobs never did.** No dates, no maturity theater, no
CTAs that dead-end behind auth, no fake screenshots, no vaporware. The product is
experimental and the site says so out loud.

Definition of done: the published site is a single cohesive dark experience that shares its
visual DNA with the shipped Living Studio, demonstrates the product rather than describing
it, and documents every surface the software actually has — with all reference content
generated from source so it cannot drift.

---

## 1. What changed since 2026-10-18 (the drift that motivates this)

Measured against `origin/main` @ `624b6857` (v0.12.0).

### 1.1 The site makes claims the product no longer supports

| The site says | `main` is |
|---|---|
| Footer "Hosted demo" → `horizon.prefect.io/…/chat` | **Correct.** 307 → WorkOS sign-in. Auth-gated by design. |
| "Hosted credentials come from the maintainers … requires a free Prefect account" | **Correct.** Hosted MCP is the Prefect deployment. |
| — | The site never mentions the **hosted Studio** as a first-class destination, nor the **hosted MCP endpoint** as a distinct thing from the hosted chat. Three hosted surfaces, two links. |
| `README.md` linked from the site | `main`'s README no longer mentions Prefect; the site still leads with it. |

**Correction to the earlier session note:** the Prefect deployment is *not* stale. It is the
deployment for the hosted MCP server, used for testing and verifying MCP, and it is
orthogonal to the Studio's local MCP bundle. The site must present all three hosted
surfaces distinctly, and must not imply the Studio replaces the hosted MCP server.

### 1.2 The product the site fails to describe

| Shipped on `main` | Site's description |
|---|---|
| Chat-first Living Studio: one room, transcript + composer never leave the screen, Rail + Lens, first-run wizard, feature flags, changelog drawer, catch-up notifications | "The Living Studio shows the Opportunity Landscape, Universal Job Map, and Impact Simulation" |
| Agent composes surfaces inline from a closed catalog — 9 primitives + 6 ODI cards | Not mentioned |
| 30 MCP tools, contract-tested against the live registry | "MCP server tools for jobs/steps/outcomes…" (vague) |
| 17 connector presets (Notion, Gong, Fireflies, Intercom, Confluence, PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Exa, Tavily, Linear, GitHub, Jira, Miro, Figma, Slack) | "connectors" (vague) |
| Tauri 2 desktop app | Not mentioned |
| Prebuilt Linux/macOS/Windows binaries via `install.sh` | Not mentioned |
| CLI: local-first, interactive chat, entity CRUD, `schema`, `score`, `connectors` | "CLI outcomes" (vague) |
| Hosted Studio on Cloudflare Workers + PR previews | One buried sentence |

### 1.3 Defects in the current build

- Copy buttons are **dead**: HTML uses `.copy_btn`, `main.js` queries `.copy-btn`.
- The scroll-reveal observer adds a `.revealed` class that **no CSS rule defines** — the
  effect is a no-op.
- **Dark mode is broken**: the page hardcodes light-mode hex values inline
  (`#1d1d1f`, `#6e6e73`, `#0062c4`, `#f5f5f7`, `#0071e3`) that never adapt.
- **Three conflicting palettes** in play: CSS custom properties, inline HTML hex, and the
  OG-art palette. They share no colors.
- `<title>` is `"Agentic ODI — Agentic ODI"`. The meta description is a **truncated
  sentence** — `"Agentic ODI explores how the Model Context Protocol"`.
- The `<h1>` sits **above** `<header>`, outside every landmark.
- `--color-bg-dark` / `--color-fg-dark` are declared and never used; the dark scheme
  swaps the light tokens in place instead.
- `.grid` and `.s-0`…`.s-7` exist in CSS and are never used.

### 1.4 Site-contract drift

`website/index.html` is **generated by `website/tools/sync-readme.py`**, which embeds the
entire page as Python string literals. The copy, the sections, and the honesty contract
are therefore pinned in a build script, and the site's headline claim is derived from
"the first prose line of the README, cut at the first `(`" — which is why the description
is truncated.

---

## 2. Decisions

All seven were settled in session on 2026-10-22. They are binding.

| # | Decision | Choice | Rejected alternative |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Architecture | Python static-site generator (Jinja2 + markdown-it-py + Pygments). **No Node in the Pages path.** | Hand-written HTML (drifts); Astro (still needs a Python extraction step, adds a second toolchain) |
| 2 | Scope | Landing + full docs hub | Landing only; docs + changelog |
| 3 | Hero centerpiece | **Interactive scripted demo** in a device frame | Static renders; both |
| 4 | Theme | **Dark-only**, sharing the Studio's tokens | True dual theme |
| 5 | Audience | **Dual — PM first, developer quickstart immediately after** | Developer-first; PM-only |
| 6 | Copy | Keep H1 + sub + the three problem beats **verbatim**; refresh "How it works" and "Status" | Full rewrite; keep everything |
| 7 | Domain | Stay on `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/` | Custom domain |

### 2.1 Why a Python generator, given GitHub Pages

GitHub Pages has **no runtime**. The constraint is on the *output* (static files), not on
the tooling: a build step runs in Actions and uploads the artifact. All three candidate
architectures are Pages-legal. The deciding factor is **anti-drift**.

The docs hub's reference content lives in Python source: 30 MCP tools
(`packages/core/.../contract.py`), the CLI command tree (`apps/cli/.../cli.py`), 17
connector presets (`packages/connectors/.../catalog.py`), the ODI entity schema
(`packages/core/.../schema.py`). Astro or Vite would **still** need a Python script to
extract that, then a JSON handoff into a second toolchain. One language, one lockfile, one
CI path.

This is also a pattern the repo has already proven: `make_og.py` renders `og.png`, the PNG
is committed, and `test_make_og.py` asserts the committed bytes are pixel-identical to a
fresh render. The same pattern scales to the whole site, and it matches the repo's other
committed-generated-artifact precedent (`apps/studio/src/api/schema.d.ts`, written by
`npm run gen:api-types`).

**The Studio is untouched.** React 19 + Vite + TypeScript stay exactly as they are.

### 2.2 Reuse, concretely

Every reference surface on the site is generated from an authoritative source. The site
cannot drift from the product, because the site *is* the product's source, rendered.

| Site content | Source of truth | Drift possible? |
|---|---|---|
| MCP tool reference (30 tools) | `packages/core/.../contract.py` `TOOL_SPECS` (already contract-tested against the live FastMCP registry) | No |
| Connector catalog (17 presets) | `packages/connectors/.../catalog.py` | No |
| ODI entity JSON schema | `packages/core/.../schema.py` | No |
| Opportunity formula | `packages/core/.../models.py` | No (already test-pinned) |
| CLI command tree | `apps/cli/.../cli.py` (Typer registry) | No |
| All guide prose | `docs/*.md`, rendered verbatim | No |
| Palette, type scale, radii, easings | `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` — **read one-way, Studio unchanged** | No |
| Install / quickstart blocks | `README.md` | No |
| License / status | `LICENSE`, `README.md` | No |

---

## 3. Goals / Non-Goals / Anti-Goals

### Goals

1. Make the product **legible in one screen**: a PM lands cold and understands what this
   is, in the time it takes to read a headline.
2. **Demonstrate, not describe.** The hero proves the thesis by running it.
3. Carry **every detail a user needs** — the landing narrative plus a complete docs hub
   and a generated API reference.
4. Look like the product. The site and the Studio share one palette, one type scale, one
   motion language, so the site reads as the front door of the Living Studio.
5. **Never lie.** Every number, name, and link is generated from or verified against
   source.

### Non-Goals

- A blog, a changelog feed, search, i18n, analytics, cookies, or a CMS.
- A custom domain (decision 7).
- Any change to the Studio's stack, architecture, or runtime behavior.
- Rebuilding the product's design system. The site **consumes** it.

### Anti-Goals

- **No vaporware.** No fake screenshots. The demo is scripted and says so.
- **No dates, no milestones, no roadmap theater.** The roadmap is checkmarks of shipped
  work only.
- **No dead ends.** Every CTA resolves: local quickstart, hosted Studio, GitHub, Issues.
  Auth-gated surfaces are labeled *before* the click, never after.
- **No emoji.** House rule, unchanged.
- **No invented testimonials, logos, customer counts, or benchmarks.**
- **No third-party requests.** No webfonts, no CDN, no analytics, no social scripts.
- **No invented auth schemes.** Never document a token header we do not have.

---

## 4. Audience & Jobs-to-be-Done

**Primary — product managers / innovation leads.** Landing cold from a link. Skeptical of
AI-tool marketing.
> When I open this page from a link in Slack, I want to see a real product doing a real
> thing within one screen, so I can decide to spend five minutes on it or leave without
> guilt.

**Secondary — AI/agent developers.** Evaluating what to wire an agent to.
> When I'm deciding what context to give my agents, I want the exact endpoint, the exact
> tool names, and a copy-paste quickstart that works locally, so I can try it without
> talking to anyone.

**Tertiary — the sharing PM.** Forwarding the link to a team or a boss.
> When I forward this page, I want it to frame the thesis — evidence over opinion —
> credibly and soberly, so the conversation starts from the idea.

---

## 5. Design system

Dark-only. The site reads as the front door of the Living Studio, so it uses the Studio's
own tokens verbatim. `website/tools/extract.py` parses
`apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` and emits `website/dist/assets/tokens.css`. **One-way
read: the Studio is never modified.**

### 5.1 Tokens

```css
:root {
  color-scheme: dark;

  --bg:          #0a0b0e;   /* canvas */
  --bg-raised:   #0e1014;   /* panels */
  --bg-sunken:   #060709;   /* wells, code */
  --text:        #f1f2f4;
  --muted:       #a2a7b3;
  --faint:       #71767f;

  --accent:        #8b8cf8;
  --accent-strong: #6366f1;
  --accent-ink:    #0a0b0e;  /* text on an accent fill */
  --green:       #4ade80;
  --amber:       #f0b34a;
  --red:         #f87171;

  --line:         rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07);
  --line-strong:  rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14);
  --surface:      rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.03);
  --surface-hover:rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);
  --glass:        rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.045);
  --glass-blur:   blur(20px) saturate(180%);
  --hairline:     inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06);

  --ease-out:     cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
  --ease-spring:  cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.22);
  --ease-tactile: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1);

  --font: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
  --mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace;

  --r-sm: 8px;  --r-md: 12px;  --r-lg: 16px;
  --r-xl: 22px; --r-pill: 999px;

  --w-page: 1200px;  --w-wide: 1440px;  --w-prose: 68ch;
  --gutter:   clamp(20px, 5vw, 48px);
  --section-y: clamp(96px, 13vw, 200px);
}
```

Spacing is a 4px scale expressed per-component (the Studio has no formal scale and the
site does not need one). Radii mirror the Studio's set.

### 5.2 Type

Zero webfonts — system stack only, same as the Studio.

| Role | Size | Weight / tracking |
|---|---|---|
| Display (hero) | `clamp(2.75rem, 7.5vw, 6rem)` | 600, `-0.04em`, lh 0.98 |
| H2 | `clamp(1.875rem, 4vw, 3.25rem)` | 600, `-0.03em`, lh 1.06 |
| H3 | `clamp(1.25rem, 2vw, 1.75rem)` | 600, `-0.02em`, lh 1.15 |
| Lead | `clamp(1.0625rem, 1.5vw, 1.375rem)` | 400, lh 1.5, `--muted` |
| Body | `1.0625rem` | 400, lh 1.65 |
| Small | `0.9375rem` | 400, lh 1.6 |
| Eyebrow / label | `0.6875rem` | 600, `0.18em`, uppercase, `--faint` |
| Code | `0.9375rem` mono | lh 1.55 |

The Studio's `hero__line` uses weight 600 with `-0.03em`; the site scales that up rather
than inventing a new voice.

### 5.3 Layout

- Page width `--w-page` (1200px); wide sections `--w-wide` (1440px); prose `--w-prose` (68ch).
- Section padding-block `--section-y`.
- Hairline borders only. Radius `--r-md` cards, `--r-lg` panels, `--r-xl` composer-style
  pills, `--r-pill` chips.
- One idea per screen. A section is a screen, not a wall.

### 5.4 Signature moves

1. **Depth without imagery.** The canvas carries the Studio's own two radial indigo
   gradients (`radial-gradient(760px 420px at 50% 108%, rgba(99,102,241,.09), …)` and
   `radial-gradient(900px 520px at 68% -12%, rgba(99,102,241,.08), …)`).
2. **Glass.** `--glass` + `--glass-blur` + `--hairline` top highlight on the hero frame,
   the demo frame, and the sticky header.
3. **Scroll-linked lens reveals.** Surfaces dock beside the narrative as you scroll —
   the Studio's own Rail + Lens metaphor, applied to the page.
4. **The formula as typography.** `Opportunity = Importance + max(Importance − Satisfaction, 0)`
   rendered as a real equation, gap term in `--accent`, with an animated
   importance/satisfaction gap bar.
5. **The six ODI cards, rendered for real.** Not screenshots — faithful recreations of
   the shipped `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts` cards in the site's CSS.
6. **Terminal-dark code.** Code is always dark (`--bg-sunken`), with working copy buttons.

### 5.5 Motion

| Element | Motion |
|---|---|
| Hero entrance | eyebrow → H1 → sub → CTAs, fade-up + `blur(2px) → blur(0)`, 700ms `--ease-out`, 90ms stagger |
| Section reveal | opacity 0→1, `translateY(24px) → 0`, 800ms `--ease-out`, `IntersectionObserver` at 15% |
| Buttons | 150ms `--ease-tactile`; hover `translateY(-1px)`, active `scale(.98)` |
| Demo typing | caret blink 1s `steps(1)` infinite |
| Demo surface | materialize, 600ms `--ease-spring` |
| Copy button | label → "Copied" for 1.5s, announced via `aria-live="polite"` |

**No-JS safety:** content is **visible by default**. The observer *opts content into* the
hidden state only after it loads, so a reader without JS never sees hidden text.

**`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`:** every transform, stagger, and reveal is removed;
content is immediate.

---

## 6. Information architecture

```
/                        landing
/docs/                   hub index
/docs/cli/               ← docs/cli.md
/docs/mcp/               ← GENERATED: 30 tools, signatures, arguments
/docs/connectors/        ← docs/connectors.md + GENERATED 17-preset table
/docs/studio/            ← docs/living-studio.md
/docs/architecture/      ← docs/architecture/README.md + data-flow.md
/docs/deployment/        ← docs/deployment.md
/docs/installation/      ← docs/installation.md
/docs/local-llm/         ← docs/local-llm.md
/docs/development/       ← docs/development.md
/docs/roadmap/           ← docs/roadmap.md
/404.html                self-contained
/sitemap.xml  /robots.txt
```

- Every path is **relative** so the site works under the project-Pages base
  `/agentic-odi/`, on a local static server, and on any future domain. `og:url`,
  `og:image`, and `rel=canonical` are **absolute**.
- Each docs page ends with a **"Source of truth: `docs/cli.md` — view on GitHub"** link,
  so the repo stays visibly authoritative. The site is a rendering, not a fork.
- `404.html` is fully self-contained (inline styles, absolute home link) because Pages
  serves it at arbitrary depths where relative assets break.
- `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt` are added — the site is now multi-page, so the
  single-page era's "no sitemap" ruling is reversed.

---

## 7. The landing page

Section IDs are stable and are part of the site contract.

| # | `id` | Section | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `top` | **Hero** | Eyebrow pill `Experimental`; H1; sub; two CTAs; scroll cue |
| 2 | `studio` | **The Living Studio** | The interactive scripted demo (§8) |
| 3 | `problem` | **Opinion is expensive.** | The three existing beats, verbatim |
| 4 | `insight` | **Ask for outcomes, not opinions.** | The formula + animated gap + 86% attribution |
| 5 | `surfaces` | **The surfaces** | The six ODI cards, rendered for real |
| 6 | `how` | **How it works** | Capture / Query / Steer — **rewritten** for the chat-first product |
| 7 | `connectors` | **Bring your own tools** | 17 connector presets, generated |
| 8 | `run` | **Run it in 60 seconds** | Install tabs, MCP config, endpoint chips, the three hosted surfaces |
| 9 | `tools` | **The MCP surface** | A peek at the 30 tools → link to the full reference |
| 10 | `status` | **Experimental** | What works today / what's next — **rewritten**, no dates |
| 11 | — | **Footer** | Mark, wordmark, tagline, links, legal |

### 7.1 Hero

- Eyebrow pill: `Experimental`
- H1: **Your roadmap is a guess.** *(verbatim — contract)*
- Sub: `An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes — and the evidence behind them.`
  *(verbatim — contract)*
- Primary CTA: **Run it in 60 seconds** → `#run`
- Secondary CTA: **Open the Living Studio** → `https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/`
- Tertiary link: **View on GitHub** → `https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi`

### 7.2 `#problem` — verbatim, contract

1. "Roadmaps set by whoever talks loudest." — Decisions default to seniority, not evidence.
2. "Features for customers who never asked." — Nobody validated the outcome; only the idea.
3. "Agents fluent in everything, grounded in nothing." — A model will confidently invent your customer.

Closer: "Add it up and the roadmap isn't a plan. It's a guess."

### 7.3 `#insight`

The three plain sentences, the formula rendered as an equation, an animated
importance/satisfaction gap bar, and the stat callout:
**86%** innovation success rate — *as reported in ODI literature (Strategyn)*.

The formula is **pinned to the code**: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py` must
contain `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`, and the page must contain
`importance+max(importance-satisfaction,0)` (whitespace-stripped, lowercased). This test
already exists and must keep passing.

### 7.4 `#surfaces` — the six ODI cards

Rendered from `apps/studio/src/ui/catalog.ts`. The six ODI cards are:

| Card | Shows |
|---|---|
| `outcome-card` | A desired outcome with importance / satisfaction / opportunity |
| `opportunity-board` | Several scored outcomes, ranked by opportunity |
| `impact-simulation` | Before / after for a proposed bet |
| `evidence-quote` | A customer quote with its provenance |
| `job-map` | The steps of a job-to-be-done |
| `decision-record` | A decision and the evidence behind it |

> **Naming note.** These are the *agent's* catalog cards, a stable contract. They are
> deliberately distinct from the Studio's canvas *view* names, which are in flux (see
> §13, Risk 2). The site names catalog cards, never view names.

### 7.5 `#how` — rewritten

The 2026-10-18 "Capture / Query / Steer" no longer describes the product. New triad:

1. **Talk.** One room. Describe a job or paste what a customer said — the studio
   captures jobs, steps, and desired outcomes from plain language, with importance and
   satisfaction you can adjust by hand.
2. **Ask.** Any agent calls the same MCP tools the studio uses — job maps, outcomes,
   evidence, opportunity scores — at decision time.
3. **Steer.** The team decides from the same picture: scored outcomes, opportunity
   boards, and bet simulations, composed inline by the agent.

### 7.6 `#run` — rewritten

- Prerequisites: Python 3.10+ and `uv`; or a prebuilt binary (Linux / macOS / Windows).
- **Install tabs** (real tabs, keyboard accessible):
  - `uv workspace` — `git clone` / `uv sync --all-packages` / `npm --prefix apps/studio run build` / `python scripts/dev.py`
  - `binary` — `curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh`
- MCP client config snippet (local only).
- **Endpoint chips**, each with a copy button and a label that says what it is:
  | Endpoint | URL | State |
  |---|---|---|
  | MCP server (local) | `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | runs with `scripts/dev.py` |
  | Living Studio (local) | `http://127.0.0.1:8100` | runs with `scripts/dev.py` |
  | Hosted MCP server | `https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp` | **auth required** — credentials from the maintainers |
  | Hosted Studio | `https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/` | public UI; live data needs the sidecar |
  | Test chat (hosted MCP) | `https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat` | **requires a free Prefect account** |
- The `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` endpoint is **linked** as the hosted MCP server (the
  2026-10-18 spec ruled it out as a 401 dead end; the 2026-10-22 correction is that it is
  the real hosted MCP deployment, and the site labels it as auth-gated *before* the
  click). Credentials are requested through **GitHub Issues** — never an invented header
  scheme.

### 7.7 `#status` — rewritten, no dates

- `Experimental` badge.
- **What works today** — generated where possible: the 30 MCP tools by name, the six
  catalog cards, the 17 connector presets, the CLI's local-first CRUD, the SQLite store,
  the Tauri desktop app, the hosted Studio, the hosted MCP server.
- **What's next** — the *unchecked* items from `docs/roadmap.md` only, or, when the
  roadmap is fully checked, an explicit "nothing queued — open an issue" line. **Never a
  date.**
- Standing line: **We don't publish dates.**
- Closer: **Questions? Open an issue.**

---

## 8. The interactive demo

The credibility gap the site cannot close with a static image: the repo has **no
screenshots**. The demo is the substitute, and it must be honest about being one.

### 8.1 Frame

A device frame — a browser-less app window, since the Studio is a Tauri desktop app —
rendering the Studio's exact chrome:

- The `.bar`: wordmark left, health pill right.
- The transcript area.
- The `.composer__shell` pill: rounded 22px, `--surface` fill, 34px circular send button.

Backed by `--glass` + `--glass-blur` + a 1px `--line-strong` hairline, with a deep shadow
(`0 40px 120px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.85)`) so it floats off the canvas.

### 8.2 Script

Three exchanges, selectable by suggestion chips (real `<button>`s) or by typing. Each ends
with the agent composing a real catalog card.

| # | Prompt | Composed card |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "A customer told us they still reconcile invoices by hand every Friday." | `outcome-card` — importance 8, satisfaction 3, opportunity 13.0 |
| 2 | "Which of these should we build first?" | `opportunity-board` — three ranked outcomes |
| 3 | "Show me the job behind that." | `job-map` — four steps of the job-to-be-done |

The agent "types" with a blinking caret, then the card materializes on `--ease-spring`.
The data is plausible and internally consistent, and the opportunity score is computed
with the **real formula** so the numbers are not decorative.

### 8.3 Honesty

Immediately above the frame:

> **Scripted preview.** These are canned responses from a fixed script. The live Studio
> talks to a real MCP server.

with a **"Open the live Studio"** link beside it. This is a hard requirement, not a
nicety: a demo that looks real but isn't is the single most damaging thing this site
could ship.

### 8.4 Constraints

- **No network calls.** No fetch, no analytics, no external requests.
- **No-JS fallback:** the demo degrades to a **static, fully readable transcript** of the
  three exchanges, with the composed cards rendered server-side. The page is complete
  and useful without JavaScript.
- Keyboard operable: chips are buttons; the composer is a real `<textarea>`; `Enter`
  submits, `Shift+Enter` newlines.
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`: the typing and materializing become instant.
- The script lives in `website/content/demo.yaml` so it is editable without touching JS.

---

## 9. The docs hub

### 9.1 Verbatim mirroring, plus a web-native layer

Guide prose is rendered **verbatim** from `docs/*.md`. One source of truth, zero drift.
On top of that, the hub adds what a web reader needs and a repo file cannot provide:

- A **hub index** grouping the guides by job: *Get started* (Quick start, Installation,
  Living Studio, Local LLM), *Build* (CLI, Connectors, MCP reference, Architecture),
  *Operate* (Deployment, Development, Roadmap).
- **A Quick start page** — a web-native path from zero to a running studio, assembled
  from `README.md` and `docs/installation.md`, with the install tabs.
- **The generated reference** (§10).
- **Web navigation** — a persistent sidebar on docs pages, plus prev/next.
- **A "source of truth" link** on every page.

### 9.2 Markdown pipeline

`markdown-it-py` with `html=False` (no raw HTML pass-through from repo docs — XSS-safe
by construction), `linkify=True`, and tables enabled. Fenced code blocks are highlighted
server-side with **Pygments** using a dark style, so highlighting costs **zero client-side
JavaScript**.

Heading anchors are generated with GitHub-compatible slugs, so a link into a doc page's
heading works.

### 9.3 The `docs/living-studio.md` problem

`docs/living-studio.md` is 360 lines of desktop/Tauri detail — correct but dense. The hub
gives it a **Studio landing page** in front of it that orients the reader (what it is,
the three run modes, the first-run flow) before the reference detail.

---

## 10. Generated reference (the anti-drift contract)

### 10.1 MCP tools

Source: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/contract.py` — `ToolName` (30 tools) and
`TOOL_SPECS` (arguments + required), which is already asserted against the live FastMCP
registry by `tests/contract`. The generator additionally introspects the live registry for
**types and defaults**, so the rendered signature is the real one.

Each tool renders as: name, one-line purpose (from a curated map in the generator, keyed
by tool name), the signature with typed parameters, and the argument table.

### 10.2 Connectors

Source: `packages/connectors/src/agentic_odi_connectors/catalog.py` — 17 presets with
their capability `area` (`voice-of-customer`, `quantitative-data`, `market-intelligence`,
`strategy-alignment`, `knowledge-output`). Renders as a filterable-by-area table.

### 10.3 CLI

Source: `apps/cli/src/agentic_odi_cli/cli.py` — introspected through Typer's registered
commands and sub-typers. Renders the command tree with help text.

### 10.4 ODI schema

Source: `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/schema.py` — `odi_schema`. Renders the
canonical JSON schema for every entity, with a copy button.

### 10.5 The guard

A test asserts the site's rendered reference **equals** the source, per surface. If a tool
is added upstream and the site is not rebuilt, CI fails. This is the guarantee that makes
the site trustworthy.

---

## 11. Copy contract

Strings the test suite pins (case-insensitively) — the existing honesty contract, plus
the new one:

| Contract | Source |
|---|---|
| `experimental` | status + eyebrow |
| `your roadmap is a guess.` | hero H1 |
| `we don't publish dates` | status section |
| `all rights reserved` | footer legal |
| `strategyn` | the 86% attribution |
| `free prefect account` | the hosted test-chat label |
| `open an issue` | status + credentials path |
| `http://localhost:8000/mcp` | the local MCP endpoint |
| `scripted preview` | **new** — the demo's honesty label |
| `requires a free prefect account` | **new** — exact label, not the truncated form |

**Forbidden** (unchanged): `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` as an *unlabeled* link, `discord`,
`mailto:`, any `Q1`–`Q4`, any `Month 20XX`, any emoji.

**Voice:** warm, direct, second person. Plain language. No jargon dumps. No superlatives
("revolutionary", "seamless", "enterprise-grade"). English only. No emoji.

---

## 12. Accessibility, performance, and the test contract

### 12.1 Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)

- Semantic landmarks (`header` / `nav` / `main` / `footer`); **exactly one `<h1>` per
  page**, inside `<main>`; no skipped heading levels.
- `lang="en"`, viewport meta, a skip link to `#main`.
- Contrast: every text pair ≥ 4.5:1, every UI boundary ≥ 3:1, on `--bg`, `--bg-raised`,
  and `--bg-sunken`. The Studio's own palette is not automatically AA on `--faint`
  (`#71767f` on `#0a0b0e` ≈ 4.0:1) — the site uses `--faint` **only** for large text and
  non-essential decoration, and uses `--muted` (`#a2a7b3`, ≈ 7.4:1) for small body text.
  This is a deliberate, documented deviation from the app's usage.
- Full keyboard operability. Focus ring: 2px `--accent` with 2px offset, never removed.
- Copy controls are real `<button>`s with accessible names; "Copied" announced via
  `aria-live="polite"`.
- Decorative SVG `aria-hidden="true"`; meaningful SVG carries `role="img"` + `<title>`.
- The demo's transcript and the docs' prose are readable with JavaScript disabled.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` fully honored.
- Tested at 360px width with no horizontal scroll.

### 12.2 Performance

- **Zero third-party requests. Zero webfonts. Zero analytics. Zero cookies.** The page
  talks only to its own origin.
- Budget per page: HTML ≤ 60 KB, CSS ≤ 40 KB, JS ≤ 25 KB total, total transfer
  ≤ 200 KB. `og.png` ≤ 300 KB.
- No layout thrash: reveals use `transform` and `opacity` only.
- Lighthouse ≥ 95 across Performance / Accessibility / Best Practices / SEO.

### 12.3 Test contract

| File | Asserts |
|---|---|
| `test_site.py` | Per-page structure, meta tags, one `h1`, landmarks, anchors resolve, honesty strings, no dates, no emoji, external-link allowlist, relative-path correctness at every depth |
| `test_design_system.py` | Tokens present and correct, type scale, `focus-visible`, `prefers-reduced-motion`, no hardcoded hex outside the token file |
| `test_generated.py` | Build determinism (two builds → identical bytes); committed `website/dist/` matches a fresh build |
| `test_content_sync.py` | Site's tool list ≡ `contract.py`; presets ≡ `catalog.py`; CLI ≡ Typer; formula ≡ `models.py`; docs pages exist for every `docs/*.md` |
| `test_make_og.py` | Deterministic render; committed PNGs pixel-identical; size budget |
| `test_pages_deploy.py` | The deploy workflow's contract, updated for the build step |

`test_sync_readme.py` and `website/tools/sync-readme.py` are **retired** — the generator
supersedes them.

---

## 13. Repo layout

```
website/
  templates/
    base.html            # shell: head, header, footer, skip link
    landing.html         # the landing page
    doc.html             # a docs page (markdown body + sidebar + prev/next)
    reference.html       # a generated reference page
    404.html             # self-contained
  content/
    landing.yaml         # structured landing copy
    demo.yaml            # the demo script
    nav.yaml             # the docs hub navigation
  assets/
    style.css            # the design system (hand-written)
    main.js              # progressive enhancement: reveal, copy, tabs
    demo.js              # the scripted demo
    mark.svg  favicon.svg
  tools/
    build_site.py        # the generator
    extract.py           # read tokens, tools, connectors, CLI, schema from source
    make_og.py           # OG card + favicon generator (repainted)
  tests/                 # the contract above
  dist/                  # GENERATED, committed, drift-gated
```

- `website/dist/` holds the built site. It is **committed** (matching the repo's existing
  precedent for `og.png` and `schema.d.ts`) and CI fails if it drifts from a fresh build.
  `.gitignore` gains `!website/dist/` because the root `dist/` pattern would otherwise
  swallow it.
- `website/tests/` and `website/tools/` never reach the Pages artifact.

---

## 14. Build & deploy

**`.github/workflows/pages.yml`**

```
checkout → setup → pytest (website) → build_site.py → rsync website/dist/ _site/
        → configure-pages → upload-pages-artifact → deploy-pages
```

`actions/upload-pages-artifact` and `actions/deploy-pages` are unchanged. The build step
is added; the artifact root moves from `website/` to `website/dist/`.

**`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — the `website` job gains a **drift check**:
`uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --check` fails when the committed `dist/`
differs from a fresh build. The `ci-green` aggregator is unchanged.

---

## 15. Risks & Mitigations

1. **The site contradicts in-flight Studio work.** An approved "Intent-First PM
   Experience" spec (local, unmerged) renames canvas views — *Opportunity Landscape* →
   *Opportunity Thesis* — and adds a "What I've learned" memory panel.
   **Mitigation:** the site names **catalog cards** (a stable contract), never canvas
   view names, and generates all product surface content from source. Narrative copy
   stays at the framework level. See §16.
2. **The generated reference goes stale.** **Mitigation:** `test_content_sync.py` fails
   CI on drift. The generator is the only way to change the site.
3. **The docs hub is a wall of text.** **Mitigation:** the hub index groups by job, a
   web-native Quick start leads, and `docs/living-studio.md` gets an orienting page.
4. **A demo that looks real but isn't.** **Mitigation:** the "Scripted preview" label is
   a test-pinned contract string, above the frame, beside a live link.
5. **Markdown rendering mangles the repo docs** (tables, nested lists, long code
   fences). **Mitigation:** render the full `docs/` corpus in the generator and diff
   against expectations; `markdown-it-py` with `html=False` handles all constructs
   present in `docs/`.
6. **A second source of truth creeps in.** **Mitigation:** no prose is written twice. The
   only hand-written copy is `website/content/*.yaml` for the landing page; every guide
   is rendered from `docs/`.
7. **Relative paths break at depth.** **Mitigation:** the generator computes a `depth`
   per page and prefixes every asset and link. `test_site.py` asserts each page's links
   resolve on disk.
8. **A pre-existing repo test fails** —
   `apps/studio-api/tests/test_studio_connectors_router.py::test_unknown_route_is_404`
   fails on a clean `main` (the SPA fallback returns 200 for unknown `/api` routes).
   **Not caused by this work and deliberately left alone**; noted so it is not
   misattributed.

---

## 16. Relationship to the in-flight "Intent-First PM Experience" work

An approved-but-unimplemented design (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-intent-first-pm-experience-design.md`)
moves the Studio toward a PM-first, intent-first product: the **Opportunity Thesis**
replaces the Opportunity Landscape as the central artifact, ODI vocabulary retreats
behind an expert view, and a "What I've learned" memory panel is added.

That work is **not in scope for this site redesign**, and the site is built against
`main` as it stands. But the site must not contradict it. Three rules follow:

1. The site names **catalog cards** — `outcome-card`, `opportunity-board`,
   `impact-simulation`, `evidence-quote`, `job-map`, `decision-record` — which are the
   agent's closed catalog and a stable contract. It does **not** name canvas views.
2. The site keeps the **ODI thesis** at the top: the framework is the engine, the
   product is the interface. That framing is compatible with intent-first, which
   explicitly keeps "ODI as the engine, never the greeting."
3. Any product-surface fact on the site is **generated from source**, so when
   intent-first lands and renames a view, the site follows on the next build rather
   than contradicting it.

The local WIP that backed this decision is preserved on the branch
`wip/preserve-local-work-2026-10-22`.

---

## 17. Resolved Questions

1. **Architecture** → Python generator, no Node in the Pages path. Astro rejected: it
   still needs a Python extraction step for the MCP/CLI/connector reference.
2. **Scope** → landing + full docs hub. The 2026-10-18 "not a docs site" ruling is
   reversed: the brief now demands "any and all details".
3. **Hero** → interactive scripted demo, labeled, with a no-JS static fallback.
4. **Theme** → dark-only. The Studio is dark-only; the site's light mode was broken.
5. **Audience** → dual, PM first.
6. **Copy** → keep the thesis and the three beats verbatim; refresh "How it works" and
   "Status".
7. **Domain** → stay on `alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/`.
8. **Prefect** → **not stale.** It is the hosted MCP deployment, used for testing and
   verifying MCP, orthogonal to the Studio's bundled local MCP. The site presents all
   three hosted surfaces distinctly and labels the auth-gated ones *before* the click.
9. **Generated output** → committed, drift-gated. Matches the repo's `og.png` and
   `schema.d.ts` precedent.
10. **Pre-existing failure** → `test_unknown_route_is_404` fails on clean `main`;
    out of scope, documented, left alone.

## 18. What's Left to the Builder

Exact micro-copy within the contract strings; per-component spacing; animation timing
within the stated curves; device-frame geometry; illustration detail for the six cards;
breakpoint tuning; the demo script's canned data (must be internally consistent and
formula-correct); the curated one-line purpose map for the 30 MCP tools.

# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

# GitHub Pages Redesign Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Replace the stale single-page GitHub Pages site with a state-of-the-art, dark, product-grade site: a landing page with an interactive scripted demo of the Living Studio, plus a full docs hub and a generated API reference — all rendered from a Python static-site generator so nothing can drift from the product source.

**Architecture:** A Python generator (`website/tools/build_site.py`) reads the repo's authoritative sources — `apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css` (design tokens), `packages/core/.../contract.py` (MCP tools), `packages/connectors/.../catalog.py` (connectors), `apps/cli/.../cli.py` (CLI tree), `packages/core/.../schema.py` (ODI schema), `docs/*.md` (guides), `README.md` (install) — and renders Jinja2 templates into `website/dist/`. The output is committed and CI-gated for drift. No Node in the Pages path. The Studio is never modified.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.10+, Jinja2 3.1.6, markdown-it-py 4.2.0, Pygments 2.21.0, Pillow 12.3.0 (OG art), pytest 9.1.1. Zero runtime dependencies on the published site: no webfonts, no CDN, no analytics, no framework runtime.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-22-github-pages-redesign-design.md` — the plan argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it.

## Global Constraints

- **Never modify `apps/studio/**`.** The site reads the Studio's theme one-way; the Studio is not a dependency of the site build and changes not at all.
- **No hardcoded hex outside `website/dist/assets/tokens.css`.** Every other color is a `var(--…)` reference.
- **No third-party requests.** Zero webfonts, zero CDN, zero analytics, zero cookies, zero social scripts.
- **Relative asset and link paths** on every page (the site lives under `/agentic-odi/`); `og:url`, `og:image`, and `rel=canonical` are absolute.
- **Exactly one `<h1>` per page**, inside `<main>`. No skipped heading levels. `header`/`nav`/`main`/`footer` landmarks present.
- **No emoji anywhere.** No dates (`Q1`–`Q4`, `Month 20XX`). No superlatives.
- **Pinned copy strings** (case-insensitive, must appear): `experimental`, `your roadmap is a guess.`, `we don't publish dates`, `all rights reserved`, `strategyn`, `free prefect account`, `open an issue`, `http://localhost:8000/mcp`, `scripted preview`, `requires a free prefect account`.
- **Forbidden strings:** `discord`, `mailto:`, and `agentic-odi.fastmcp.app` appearing without the auth-required label adjacent to it.
- **Opportunity formula** must render as `importance+max(importance-satisfaction,0)` (whitespace-stripped, lowercased) to match `packages/core/src/agentic_odi_core/models.py`.
- **The three hosted surfaces are distinct** and each is labeled: local MCP `http://localhost:8000/mcp`, local Studio `http://127.0.0.1:8100`, hosted MCP `https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp` (auth required), hosted Studio `https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/`, test chat `https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat` (requires a free Prefect account).
- **The site names catalog cards, never canvas view names.** Catalog cards: `outcome-card`, `opportunity-board`, `impact-simulation`, `evidence-quote`, `job-map`, `decision-record`. Never "Opportunity Landscape" or "Opportunity Thesis".
- **Dark-only.** `color-scheme: dark`. One `theme-color` meta.
- **Content files are JSON, not YAML** — `website/content/*.json`. JSON is stdlib; no new dependency.
- **Generated output is committed.** `website/dist/` is added to git; `.gitignore` gains `!website/dist/` because the root `dist/` pattern would otherwise swallow it.
- **Verification loop for every task:** `uv run --directory website pytest tests/ -q` and `uv run --directory website mypy .` must both pass before committing.

## Review Focus

Each line is an input class or failure mode the spec implies that a naive implementation would get wrong. The test that pins each is named in the task that owns the code.

1. **A page two directories deep** (`/docs/mcp/`) — relative asset links must resolve from that depth, not only from `/`. A naive `"assets/style.css"` breaks every docs page. → `test_site.py::test_every_page_resolves_its_own_assets`
2. **JavaScript disabled** — the demo must still show a complete, readable transcript of all three exchanges, and no section may be stuck invisible. A naive reveal implementation hides content permanently. → `test_site.py::test_demo_transcript_is_server_rendered`
3. **`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`** — every reveal, stagger, and the demo's typing must become instant, and no content may remain hidden. → `test_design_system.py::test_reduced_motion_disables_all_motion`
4. **A new MCP tool added upstream** — the site's tool reference must pick it up on the next build, and CI must fail if `dist/` was not rebuilt. A hand-written list silently omits it. → `test_content_sync.py::test_site_tool_list_matches_contract`
5. **A docs page whose markdown contains a table, a nested list, and a fenced code block** — the rendering pipeline must produce a real `<table>`, a nested `<ul>`, and a highlighted `<pre>`, and must not pass raw HTML through. → `test_docs_render.py::test_markdown_features_render`
6. **A `docs/*.md` file with a heading that duplicates another file's heading** — anchors must still be unique within their page, and every in-page `#anchor` link must resolve. → `test_site.py::test_in_page_anchors_resolve`
7. **A user tabbing through the demo** — the suggestion chips and the composer must be reachable and operable, and the scripted exchange must advance without a mouse. → `test_site.py::test_demo_controls_are_buttons`
8. **A screen reader on the landing page** — the skipped `nav` landmark, the decorative background gradients, and the SVG charts must not produce noise. → `test_site.py::test_decorative_svg_is_hidden_from_assistive_tech`

---

## File Structure

```
website/
  templates/
    base.html            # shell: head, skip link, header, footer
    landing.html         # the landing page
    doc.html             # a docs page: sidebar + prose + prev/next
    reference.html       # a generated reference page
    404.html             # self-contained
  content/
    landing.json         # structured landing copy (the only hand-written prose)
    demo.json            # the demo script
    nav.json             # docs hub navigation
  assets/
    style.css            # hand-written design system
    main.js              # progressive enhancement: reveal, copy, tabs
    demo.js              # the scripted demo
    mark.svg  favicon.svg
  tools/
    build_site.py        # the generator
    extract.py           # read tokens/tools/connectors/CLI/schema from source
    make_og.py           # OG card + favicon generator (repainted)
  tests/
    test_site.py         # structure, meta, landmarks, honesty, links
    test_design_system.py# tokens, type, motion, focus
    test_generated.py    # build determinism + committed output freshness
    test_content_sync.py # site ≡ source for tools/connectors/CLI/formula
    test_docs_render.py  # markdown pipeline
    test_make_og.py      # OG determinism + pixel identity
    test_pages_deploy.py # deploy workflow contract
  dist/                  # GENERATED, committed, drift-gated
```

**Responsibility split:** `extract.py` is pure source-reading — it knows nothing about HTML. `build_site.py` owns rendering and knows nothing about where the data came from. Templates own markup. `assets/style.css` owns the design system. `assets/*.js` owns behavior.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `extract.py` — `read_tokens` and `read_odi_formula`**

`read_tokens` parses the **first** `:root { … }` block of the given CSS file and returns every `--name: value;` pair, values lowercased and whitespace-collapsed. It must NOT match the second `:root` block (the easings block) — stop at the first `}`. The easings block is read separately by the same function when the caller wants `--ease-*`; the site template will concatenate both blocks, so `read_tokens` returns the first block and `read_easings(studio_theme) -> dict[str, str]` returns the second.

`read_odi_formula` returns the raw source text of the line in `models.py` containing `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Implement `build_site.py` — `build()` with a Jinja2 environment**

```python
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import filecmp
import shutil
import sys
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
SITE = ROOT / "website"
TEMPLATES = SITE / "templates"
CONTENT = SITE / "content"
ASSETS = SITE / "assets"
OUT_DIR = SITE / "dist"
PAGES_URL = "https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/"
```

The environment: `Environment(loader=FileSystemLoader(TEMPLATES), autoescape=select_autoescape(["html", "xml"]), trim_blocks=True, lstrip_blocks=True)`. Autoescape is on — every interpolated value is escaped unless explicitly marked safe.

`build(out_dir, *, check=False)`:
1. Creates a Jinja `env`.
2. Renders `base.html` for each page with a context containing at minimum: `page` (dict with `title`, `description`, `path`, `depth`, `og_image`), `nav`, `content`, `depth` (int, 0 at the site root).
3. Writes `index.html`, `404.html`, `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt` into `out_dir`.
4. Copies `ASSETS/*` into `out_dir/assets/`.
5. If `check=True`: compares the freshly rendered tree against `out_dir` on disk; on any difference, prints the differing paths and raises `SystemExit(1)`. Otherwise, removes `out_dir` and writes the fresh tree.

The CLI: `python website/tools/build_site.py [--out DIR] [--check]`. `--check` must not modify anything on disk.

`robots.txt` content — exactly:
```
User-agent: *
Allow: /

Sitemap: https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/sitemap.xml
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement `templates/base.html` and `templates/404.html`**

`base.html` blocks: `{% block head %}{% endblock %}`, `{% block body %}{% endblock %}`, `{% block footer %}{% endblock %}`, with the shell (doctype, `<html lang="en">`, head meta, skip link, `<header>`, `<main id="main">`, `<footer>`).

`404.html` must be **self-contained**: inline `<style>`, no external `link`/`script`/`img` reference, an `<h1>`, and an absolute link to `https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write `website/assets/style.css`**

The full design system from the spec §5: tokens are **not** in this file (they are generated into `tokens.css`); this file holds layout, type, components, and motion.

Required structure:
- `@layer reset, base, layout, components, utilities;`
- Reset: `* { box-sizing: border-box }`, `html { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% }`, `body { margin: 0; -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased }`, `img, svg { display: block; max-width: 100% }`.
- Base: `body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--text); font-family: var(--font); }` plus the canvas gradients:
  ```css
  body::before {
    content: "";
    position: fixed;
    inset: 0;
    z-index: -1;
    background:
      radial-gradient(760px 420px at 50% 108%, rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.09), transparent 72%),
      radial-gradient(900px 520px at 68% -12%, rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.08), transparent 68%);
    pointer-events: none;
  }
  ```
- Type: the scale from spec §5.2, with `--fs-display`, `--fs-h2`, `--fs-h3`, `--fs-lead`, `--fs-body`, `--fs-small`, `--fs-label`, `--fs-code`.
- Layout: `.shell` (max-width `--w-page`, padding-inline `--gutter`), `.shell--wide` (`--w-wide`), `.prose` (`--w-prose`), `.section` (padding-block `--section-y`).
- Components: `.eyebrow`, `.btn` + `.btn--primary` + `.btn--ghost`, `.pill`, `.card`, `.glass`, `.hairline`, `.codeblock` + `.copy-btn`, `.tabs`, `.chip`, `.stat`, `.meter`, `.link-arrow`.
- Motion: the keyframes `reveal-up`, `hero-in`, `caret-blink`, `surface-in`, `shimmer`; the `--ease-*` tokens come from `tokens.css`.
- `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block setting `animation-duration: 0.001ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.001ms !important;` on `*, *::before, *::after`, plus `scroll-behavior: auto !important` on `html`.

**Color rule:** this file must contain no 6-digit hex. The two `rgba(99, 102, 241, …)` values in the body gradient are the **only** literal colors allowed, and they are named in a comment as mirroring the Studio's `--accent-strong`; alternatively express them as `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-strong) 9%, transparent)`. Prefer the `color-mix` form so the test stays strict — assert no hex **and** no `rgba(` except where a comment documents the exception. Simplest: use `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent-strong) 9%, transparent)`.

- [ ] **Step 4: Emit `assets/tokens.css` from the build**

In `build_site.build`, after rendering, write `out_dir/assets/tokens.css` containing:
1. A comment: `/* Generated from apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css. Do not edit by hand. */`
2. The Studio's `:root` block, verbatim, as extracted.
3. The Studio's easings `:root` block, verbatim.
4. A second `:root` block with the **site-only** additions listed in the Interfaces section.

The copy button reads the text of the `<code>` inside its own `<pre>`, writes it with `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, swaps the label to "Copied" for 1.5s, and announces it through a shared `aria-live="polite"` region. On clipboard failure it falls back to selecting the code text.

"""The design system: tokens come from the Studio, and nothing hardcodes colour."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import pytest

import extract
from conftest import SITE, STUDIO_THEME

STYLE = SITE / "assets" / "style.css"


def _css() -> str:
    return STYLE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_tokens_come_from_the_studio_theme():
    tokens = extract.read_tokens(STUDIO_THEME)
    assert tokens["--bg"] == "#0a0b0e"
    assert tokens["--bg-raised"] == "#0e1014"
    assert tokens["--text"] == "#f1f2f4"
    assert tokens["--muted"] == "#a2a7b3"
    assert tokens["--accent"] == "#8b8cf8"
    assert tokens["--accent-strong"] == "#6366f1"
    assert tokens["--green"] == "#4ade80"
    assert tokens["--amber"] == "#f0b34a"


def test_easings_come_from_the_studio_theme():
    easings = extract.read_easings(STUDIO_THEME)
    assert easings["--ease-apple-out"] == "cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)"
    assert easings["--ease-apple-spring"] == "cubic-bezier(0.175, 0.885, 0.32, 1.22)"
    assert easings["--ease-tactile"] == "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1)"


def test_site_css_has_no_hardcoded_hex():
    css = _css()
    assert re.findall(r"#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\b", css) == []


def test_site_css_uses_the_tokens():
    css = _css()
    for token in ("--bg", "--text", "--muted", "--accent", "--line", "--font", "--mono"):
        assert f"var({token})" in css, f"{token} is never used"


def test_focus_is_always_visible():
    css = _css()
    assert ":focus-visible" in css
    assert "outline: 2px solid var(--accent)" in css


def test_reduced_motion_disables_all_motion():
    css = _css()
    assert "prefers-reduced-motion: reduce" in css
    block = css.split("prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", 1)[1]
    assert "animation-duration: 0.001ms" in block
    assert "transition-duration: 0.001ms" in block
    assert "scroll-behavior: auto" in block


def test_the_type_scale_is_present():
    css = _css()
    assert "clamp(2.75rem, 7.5vw, 6rem)" in css        # display
    assert "clamp(1.875rem, 4vw, 3.25rem)" in css      # section title
    assert "clamp(1.0625rem, 1.5vw, 1.375rem)" in css  # lead
    assert "letter-spacing: -0.04em" in css
    assert "letter-spacing: 0.18em" in css


def test_the_layout_is_mobile_first_and_fluid():
    css = _css()
    assert "--w-page" not in css or True  # widths live in tokens.css
    assert "clamp(20px, 5vw, 48px)" in _tokens_css()  # gutter
    assert "max-width: 640px" in css
    assert "min-width: 760px" in css or "min-width: 960px" in css


def test_content_is_visible_without_javascript():
    """Reveal-on-scroll must opt *in*, never opt out.

"""The site's contract: structure, metadata, honesty, and links.

Every page the generator produces is checked here. The site is a product
surface, so the tests care about two things above all: that the structure is
honest, and that nothing on it is a dead end.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

import pytest

import extract
from conftest import CORE_MODELS_PY, all_pages, h1_text, read_page

PAGES_URL = "https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/"

# Every external origin the site may reference. Nothing else may appear.
ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_PREFIXES = (
    "https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi",
    "https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/",
    "https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/",
    "https://agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp",
    "https://horizon.prefect.io/alhase/servers/agentic-odi/chat",
    "https://docs.astral.sh/uv/",
    "https://modelcontextprotocol.io",
    "https://www.python.org/downloads/",
    "https://www.prefect.io/horizon",
    "https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp",
    "https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/",
    "https://pypi.org/project/",
)

# The strings the site must carry. These are promises, not decoration.
REQUIRED_STRINGS = (
    "experimental",
    "your roadmap is a guess.",
    "we don't publish dates",
    "all rights reserved",
    "strategyn",
    "free prefect account",
    "open an issue",
    "http://localhost:8000/mcp",
)

# Strings the site must never carry.
FORBIDDEN_STRINGS = (
    "discord",
    "mailto:",
)

EMOJI = re.compile("[\u2600-\u27bf\U0001f300-\U0001faff]")
QUARTER = re.compile(r"\bQ[1-4]\b")
MONTH_YEAR = re.compile(
    r"\b(January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+20\d\d"
)


def _meta(html: str, name: str) -> str | None:
    match = re.search(
        rf'<meta\s+(?:name|property)="{re.escape(name)}"\s+content="([^"]*)"', html
    )
    return match.group(1) if match else None


def _all_html() -> str:
    return "\n".join(read_page(page) for page in all_pages())


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- basics


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_page_has_the_required_basics(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    assert 'lang="en"' in html
    assert '<meta charset="utf-8">' in html
    assert "width=device-width" in html


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_page_has_exactly_one_h1(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    assert html.count("<h1") == 1, f"{page} must have exactly one <h1>"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_page_headings_never_skip_a_level(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    levels = [int(level) for level in re.findall(r"<h([1-6])\b", html)]
    assert levels, f"{page} has no headings"
    assert levels[0] == 1, f"{page} must start at <h1>"
    for previous, current in zip(levels, levels[1:], strict=False):
        assert current <= previous + 1, f"{page} skips from <h{previous}> to <h{current}>"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_page_has_the_landmarks(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    for landmark in ("<header", "<main", "<footer"):
        assert landmark in html, f"{page} is missing {landmark}>"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_in_page_anchors_resolve(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    ids = set(re.findall(r'id="([^"]+)"', html))
    for anchor in re.findall(r'href="#([^"]+)"', html):
        assert anchor in ids, f"{page}: #{anchor} does not resolve"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_no_third_party_requests(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    for url in re.findall(r'https?://[^"\')\s]+', html):
        assert url.startswith(ALLOWED_EXTERNAL_PREFIXES), f"{page}: unexpected {url}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_no_emoji(page: str):
    assert not EMOJI.search(read_page(page)), f"{page} contains an emoji"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_no_milestone_dates(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    assert not QUARTER.search(html), f"{page} contains a quarter"
    assert not MONTH_YEAR.search(html), f"{page} contains a month and year"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("page", all_pages())
def test_decorative_svg_is_hidden_from_assistive_tech(page: str):
    html = read_page(page)
    for tag in re.findall(r"<svg\b[^>]*>", html):
        assert "aria-hidden" in tag or "role=" in tag, f"{page}: {tag}"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- landing


def test_landing_has_exactly_one_h1_inside_main():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    assert h1_text(html) == "Your roadmap is a guess."
    main = html.split("<main", 1)[1].split("</main>", 1)[0]
    assert "<h1" in main


def test_landing_sections_have_stable_ids():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    for anchor in ("top", "problem", "insight", "run", "status"):
        assert f'id="{anchor}"' in html


def test_opportunity_formula_matches_the_core_source():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    compact = re.sub(r"\s+", "", html).lower()
    assert "importance+max(importance-satisfaction,0)" in compact


def test_the_rendered_formula_is_generated_from_the_core_source():
    # The page must not merely *contain* the formula — it must contain the
    # formula the core module actually computes, read from the source.
    source = extract.read_odi_formula(CORE_MODELS_PY)
    assert "importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)" in source
    compact = re.sub(r"\s+", "", read_page("index.html")).lower()
    assert re.sub(r"\s+", "", source).lower() in compact


def test_the_formula_is_not_typed_into_the_content_file():
    from conftest import SITE

    content = (SITE / "content" / "landing.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert "importance - satisfaction" not in content


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- metadata


def test_the_landing_carries_complete_social_metadata():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    assert _meta(html, "og:type") == "website"
    assert _meta(html, "og:site_name") == "Agentic ODI"
    assert _meta(html, "og:url") == PAGES_URL
    assert _meta(html, "og:image") == PAGES_URL + "assets/og.png"
    assert _meta(html, "twitter:card") == "summary_large_image"
    assert _meta(html, "twitter:title")
    assert _meta(html, "twitter:description")
    assert _meta(html, "twitter:image") == PAGES_URL + "assets/og.png"
    assert f'<link rel="canonical" href="{PAGES_URL}">' in html
    assert html.count('name="theme-color"') == 1


def test_the_title_and_description_are_well_formed():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    title = re.search(r"<title>(.*?)</title>", html).group(1).strip()
    assert "Agentic ODI" in title
    assert len(title) <= 60
    description = _meta(html, "description")
    assert description
    assert len(description) <= 160
    assert description.endswith(".") or description.endswith("them.")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- honesty


def test_the_required_strings_are_present():
    html = _all_html().lower()
    for string in REQUIRED_STRINGS:
        assert string in html, f"the site is missing {string!r}"


def test_the_forbidden_strings_are_absent():
    html = _all_html().lower()
    for string in FORBIDDEN_STRINGS:
        assert string not in html, f"the site contains {string!r}"


def test_the_auth_gated_surfaces_are_labeled_before_the_link():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    for url in ("agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp", "horizon.prefect.io"):
        position = html.index(url)
        window = html[position : position + 600].lower()
        assert "auth" in window or "prefect account" in window, f"{url} is not labeled"


def test_the_three_hosted_surfaces_are_distinguished():
    html = read_page("index.html")
    assert "agentic-odi.fastmcp.app/mcp" in html
    assert "agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev" in html
    assert "horizon.prefect.io" in html


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- 404


def test_the_404_page_is_self_contained():
    html = read_page("404.html")
    assert 'lang="en"' in html
    assert "<h1" in html
    assert PAGES_URL in html
    assert "<link" not in html
    assert "<script" not in html
    assert "<img" not in html

def _signature(tool: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """A tool's signature, the way the MCP server declares it."""
    parts = []
    for param in tool["params"]:
        text = param["name"]
        if param["annotation"]:
            text += f": {param['annotation']}"
        if param["default"] is not None:
            text += f" = {param['default']}"
        parts.append(text)
    return f"{tool['name']}({', '.join(parts)})"


def _works_today(
    tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
    cards: list[dict[str, str]],
    connectors: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[str]:
    """What the product actually does today.

    The counts are read from the source; the sentences are editorial.
    """
    return [
        f"{len(tools)} MCP tools over jobs, steps, desired outcomes, customer outcomes, and evidence.",
        f"{len(cards)} agent-composed surfaces, from a closed catalog the studio owns.",

def headings(html: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """The headings in a rendered page, for a table of contents."""
    found: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    seen: dict[str, int] = {}
    for match in re.finditer(r"<h([23])[^>]*>(.*?)</h\1>", html, re.DOTALL):
        level = int(match.group(1))
        text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", match.group(2)).strip()
        anchor = slugify(text)
        count = seen.get(anchor, 0)
        seen[anchor] = count + 1
        if count:
            anchor = f"{anchor}-{count}"
        found.append({"level": str(level), "text": text, "anchor": anchor})
    return found

def _flat_guides(nav: dict[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Every guide, in navigation order, with its group."""
    return [
        (group, guide)
        for group in nav.get("groups", [])
        for guide in group.get("guides", [])
    ]


def _guide_body(
    env: Environment,
    guide: dict[str, Any],
    context: dict[str, Any],
) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, str]]]:
    """A guide's rendered body and its table of contents.

    A guide with a ``source`` is rendered from the repository's markdown. The
    two without one — the quick start and the MCP reference — are generated,
    because they are joins the repository cannot express.
    """
    slug = guide["slug"]

    if slug == "quick-start":
        body = env.get_template("_quick_start.html").render(**context)
        return body, []

    if slug == "mcp":
        body = env.get_template("_mcp_reference.html").render(**context)
        return body, []

    source = guide.get("source")
    if not source:
        return "", []

    path = ROOT / source
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"the guide {source} does not exist")
    body = markdown_render.render(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), source_path=source)
    return body, markdown_render.headings(body)


def _render_docs(env: Environment, nav: dict[str, Any], context: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every docs page, keyed by its path relative to the site root."""
    guides = _flat_guides(nav)
    rendered: dict[str, str] = {}

    for index, (group, guide) in enumerate(guides):
        slug = guide["slug"]
        output = f"docs/{slug}/index.html"
        page_context = dict(context)
        page_context["nav"] = nav
        page_context["page"] = {
            "title": guide["title"],
            "description": guide.get("blurb", ""),
            "path": output,
            "depth": 2,
            "slug": slug,
            "group_title": group["title"],
            "blurb": guide.get("blurb", ""),
            "previous": guides[index - 1][1] if index else None,
            "next": guides[index + 1][1] if index + 1 < len(guides) else None,
        }
        body, toc = _guide_body(env, guide, page_context)
        page_context["page"]["body"] = body
        page_context["page"]["toc"] = toc
        page_context["prefix"] = "../../"
        rendered[output] = env.get_template("doc.html").render(**page_context)

    return rendered


def _render_docs_index(env: Environment, nav: dict[str, Any], context: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The hub index: every guide, grouped by the job it does."""
    page_context = dict(context)
    page_context["nav"] = nav
    page_context["page"] = {
        "title": "Documentation",
        "description": (
            "Every guide, the CLI reference, the connector catalog, and the full "
            "MCP tool reference."
        ),
        "path": "docs/index.html",
        "depth": 1,
        "slug": "",
        "group_title": "Documentation",
        "blurb": "",
        "previous": None,
        "next": None,
        "body": "",
        "toc": [],
    }
    page_context["prefix"] = "../"
    return env.get_template("docs_index.html").render(**page_context)


def _render_pages(env: Environment) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Render every page, returning output path -> HTML."""
    landing = _load_json("landing.json")

    connectors = extract.read_connectors(CATALOG_PY)

    context = _page_context(
        page={
            "title": SITE_NAME,

{# The quick start. The one page a repository file cannot be: it is the join between the landing page's promise and the reference's depth. #}

Four steps, from an empty machine to a running studio with an agent attached to a real MCP server. Nothing here needs an account.

  1. Get the code

    You need Python 3.10 or newer and uv. Clone the workspace and install every package in it.

    git clone https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi.git cd agentic-odi uv sync --all-packages

    Prefer a binary? The installer puts odi, odipm, odi-cli, and agentic-odi on your path for Linux, macOS, and Windows.

  2. Build the studio

    The Living Studio is a React and TypeScript app. Build it once; the server serves the built assets.

    npm --prefix apps/studio run build

  3. Run both services

    One command starts the MCP server and the studio sidecar together.

    python scripts/dev.py
    ServiceURL
    MCP serverhttp://localhost:8000/mcp
    The Living Studiohttp://127.0.0.1:8100

    For hot reload, npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together. For the desktop app, use npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev.

  4. Point an agent at it

    The server speaks the Model Context Protocol. Any MCP client can reach it.

    { "mcpServers": { "agentic-odi": { "url": "http://localhost:8000/mcp" } } }

    Every tool is listed in the MCP tool reference. The studio itself is optional — the server is the product, and the studio is one client of it.

Where to go next

  • The Living Studio — the interface, its first run, and the desktop app.
  • CLI reference — the same data from the terminal, with no server running.
  • Connectors — pull evidence in from where your customers already talk.
  • Deployment — the hosted server, the hosted studio, and previews.

def _heading_renderer(markdown: MarkdownIt) -> None:
    """Give every heading a stable anchor, the way GitHub does.

    A guide's own top-level heading is the page's title, and the template
    renders it. So a level-one heading inside the body is demoted to level
    two, and the page keeps exactly one ``<h1>``.
    """

    def render(tokens: list, index: int, options, env, **kwargs) -> str:  # noqa: ANN001
        token = tokens[index]
        level = int(token.tag[1])
        if level == 1:
            level = 2
        anchor = _unique_anchor(env, token.content)
        return f'<h{level} id="{anchor}">{token.content}</h{level}>'

    markdown.renderer.rules["heading_open"] = render

"""The site must agree with the code it documents.

These are the drift alarms. If a tool is added to the MCP server, a
connector preset to the catalog, or a command to the CLI, the site's
reference pages must change with it — and CI fails if they do not.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

import extract
from conftest import (
    CATALOG_PY,
    CATALOG_TS,
    CLI_PY,
    CONTRACT_PY,
    MCP_SERVER_PY,
    ROADMAP_MD,
    SITE,
    read_page,
)


def test_site_tool_list_matches_the_contract():
    tools = extract.read_tools(MCP_SERVER_PY, CONTRACT_PY)
    html = read_page("docs/mcp/index.html")
    for tool in tools:
        assert f'id="tool-{tool["name"]}"' in html, f"{tool['name']} is missing from the site"


def test_every_tool_signature_on_the_site_is_the_real_one():
    tools = extract.read_tools(MCP_SERVER_PY, CONTRACT_PY)
    html = read_page("docs/mcp/index.html")
    for tool in tools:
        expected = tool["name"] + "("
        assert expected in html
        for param in tool["params"]:
            assert param["name"] in html


def test_site_connector_list_matches_the_catalog():
    presets = extract.read_connectors(CATALOG_PY)
    html = read_page("index.html")
    for preset in presets:
        assert f'id="connector-{preset["id"]}"' in html, f"{preset['id']} is missing from the site"


def test_site_cli_commands_match_the_registry():
    commands = extract.read_cli(CLI_PY)
    assert commands, "no CLI commands were found"
    html = read_page("docs/cli/index.html")
    for command in commands:
        assert command["name"] in html, f"{command['name']} is missing from the site"


def test_the_catalog_cards_on_the_site_match_the_studio():
    cards = extract.read_catalog_cards(CATALOG_TS)
    html = read_page("index.html")
    for card in cards:
        assert card["type"] in html, f"{card['type']} is missing from the site"


def test_the_roadmap_page_is_rendered_from_the_repository():
    pending = extract.read_roadmap_pending(ROADMAP_MD)
    html = read_page("docs/roadmap/index.html")
    # Every checked item in the repository is a checked item on the site.
    for line in ROADMAP_MD.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if stripped.startswith("- [x]"):
            title = stripped[5:].strip().split("**")[1]
            assert title in html, f"{title!r} is missing from the roadmap page"
    assert len(pending) == 0, "the roadmap has pending items; the status copy must change"


def test_the_landing_counts_match_the_source():
    tools = extract.read_tools(MCP_SERVER_PY, CONTRACT_PY)
    connectors = extract.read_connectors(CATALOG_PY)
    cards = extract.read_catalog_cards(CATALOG_TS)
    text = read_page("index.html")
    assert f"{len(tools)} MCP tools" in text
    assert f"{len(cards)} agent-composed surfaces" in text
    assert f"{len(connectors)} connector presets" in text


def test_every_guide_in_the_navigation_exists_on_disk():
    nav = json.loads((SITE / "content" / "nav.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for group in nav["groups"]:
        for guide in group["guides"]:
            source = guide.get("source")
            if source:
                assert (SITE.parents[0] / source).is_file(), f"{source} does not exist"
